articles.summary: Kelly Somers speaks to Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard.
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 10 Oct 2026 , · 17 mins

In this week’s edition of The Football Interview, Kelly Somers speaks to Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard. They speak about last season at Arsenal, his qualities as a captain and reflects on Norway's journey at this summer's World Cup. They look at how Arsenal have already started this season, and whether they feel a different kind of pressure this time around. articles.title: The making of Keelon Russell: From his nickname to his 'old school' approach, Alabama's star QB is built a bit different for a 19-year-old
articles.summary: Despite surging into the Heisman conversation as the leader of the Crimson Tide, you probably don't know much about the kid they call El Presidente.
articles.body:
Keelon Russell does not look old school .

He eats a bag of skittles before each game, washes down the sugary snacks with Gatorade, listens to beats of Atlanta rap artist Lil Baby and can often be found playing the NBA 2K video game.

But you don't know the half of it. There's another side of Keelon Russell, the starting quarterback for the Alabama Crimson Tide. In fact, you probably don't know much about the kid they call El Presidente, the one who left a Texas high school as the second highest-ranked recruit in the country, the athletic "freak" with a rocket of an arm who's vaulted up Heisman Trophy odds .

Russell is, in fact, old school . Better yet, he's an "old soul," says his former high school offensive coordinator, Todd Peterman. He's mature well beyond his years, something Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer learned last summer after the tragic death of Keelon's twin sister, Kiersten.

Those at the funeral gathered not around an older brother or father figure, but around Keelon.

"He's been through some stuff," DeBoer told Yahoo Sports this week during an interview. "I saw a side of him that blew me away."

Keelon's maturity, his humbleness, is a product of his mom and dad, as well as one of the nation's premier quarterback trainers, Brad Frazier, a 66-year-old white-haired, bespectacled man and retired tech CEO who cruises around Frisco, Texas, in a white Hummer wrapped in an advertisement for his business.

Frazier recalls the first time he witnessed Russell throw a football as a freshman in high school. During one windy, cold day at a Dallas-area football field, Peterman arrived with two quarterbacks — one a rising sophomore Frazier had never heard of and the other a rising senior poised to be the starter that coming season for the Duncanville High Panthers, a powerhouse program in suburban south Dallas.

From the field, Peterman nudged Frazier, "I want you to really watch this freshman. He's got it ."

"He threw against a 25 mile-an-hour wind," Frazier recalls. "When you see it , you just kind of know."

Eventually, after an injury to that senior in the 2022 season opener, everyone in Duncanville saw it . It manifested into consecutive state championships, a career high school record of 42-2, more than 10,000 yards passing and 127 touchdowns. They got to see the old soul, a wiry beanpole of a quarterback cut through some of the nation's best prep defenses — even his own (he played and practiced on a team with now-Texas defensive end Colin Simmons and threw passes to Dakorien Moore, now at Oregon, and against defensive back Javion Holiday, now at SMU).

From under-recruited to Heisman contender

Keelon's on-field theatrics have now gone mainstream, which has produced their share of mispronunciations. April Moore, Keelon's mother, often reminds people that her son's name isn't pronounced KEE-Lawn. It's KEE-Lin.

Speaking of mainstream, as No. 6 Alabama (5-0) prepares to host No. 2 Georgia (5-0) in a showdown in Tuscaloosa Saturday, Russell's big-play ability has burst onto the national scene. He leads the SEC in yards per attempt (10.71) and has a whopping 48 completions of at least 10 yards. After a bumpy start — two touchdowns and three turnovers in the first two games — he's had 13 scores and zero turnovers in the last three. In fact, he became the first Alabama player in the last 30 years to account for at least 300 yards of offense, three passing touchdowns and one rushing in three consecutive games.

In a world where coaches are moving aside floundering young, highly paid quarterbacks — see Colorado, Tennessee and maybe Michigan — Russell finds himself fielding questions about the Heisman, fitting for a player whose nickname, El Presidente, derives from his leadership ability.

As you'd expect, he brushes off such talk.

"Not really worried about the Heisman right now," he told reporters after Alabama's 56-23 win at Mississippi State.

This week is different. After all, it is Georgia — Russell's toughest test yet.

In a sign of the week's magnitude, people are acting differently. For instance, Keelon's father and mother are politely declining interview requests. That goes too for one of Keelon's other quarterback trainers, Brad Stanfield, who sent to Yahoo Sports a statement noting that he did not want to "take the light off what they are building."

Keelon himself has mostly only been made available to the media for a short period after games. To tell his story, interviews from various outlets must be patched together, including his cover piece last year in the national magazine Men's Health and a 15-minute video produced by the university's internal media team, where Keelon acknowledged his obsession with the sport.

He says he emerged once from concussion protocol in high school to throw five touchdowns in a game because, he said to himself, "Screw that! I'd sacrifice everything to help my team win."

"I will die for this game," he said. "Going through rough times in my life, being able to be on the field, it brings peace to me."

Russell models his mental game off of Tom Brady. He's a film junkie, prides himself in analyzing defenses pre-snap, reading his progressions and, despite an athleticism that well surpasses Brady, standing tall in the pocket. He avoids the temptation to run.

It's an old-school mentality — all of it.

He reads scripture nightly, got re-baptized upon his arrival in Tuscaloosa last year and "is not a money person," his mom says. In fact, during the interview with Men's Health, Keelon says he intentionally "keeps it simple."

"I'm not a flashy person. I ain't even got no jewelry on," he said. "Just clothes and shoes."

Simple but serious. Don't call Russell a dual-threat quarterback. He's a quarterback who can run, too. In fact, he can run really fast. Russell joined the Duncanville track team ahead of his senior season on Peterman's insistence.

The track coach called Peterman after one of Russell's first days.

"He's a freak!" the coach yelped on the phone.

Russell ran a 48-second, 400-meter dash, and if you're not familiar with that, the average Olympic medalist time is around 45 seconds.

"There used to be this stigmatism with Black quarterbacks," Peterman said. "Me and Key had a conversation about that when I got [to Duncanville] and I said, 'Who gives a s***? Don't worry about how you are labeled. Do what you do.'"

Ryan Grubb, Alabama's offensive coordinator, delivered a message to Russell about that before this season.

"If that's all they ever say about you — that you have athletic ability — that would be an insult," Grubb said he told the quarterback. "He takes that very seriously."

Holiday, the SMU defensive back who chased down Russell at Duncanville High practices, watches him on television evade defenders with some of the same moves. He's just as lethal with his feet as he is with his arm.

"As you can see, he's getting away with tackles now. He's doing stuff," Holiday said.

In high school, recruiting sites compared Russell to former Heisman Trophy winner Jayden Daniels. For DeBoer, Russell most reminds him of a cross between two quarterbacks he's coached: Michael Penix and his starter last year, Ty Simpson.

During a call on Tuesday, DeBoer moves through his quarterback's abilities one by one: deep ball, quick release, escape speed, good instincts and feel.

In a comment not to be under-appreciated , the coach says, "With him, you expect the throw that you probably didn't think can be made. But he makes it."

It's why Peterman and Frazier nearly blew a fuse when Russell's college recruitment started so slowly.

So under-recruited as a junior, Keelon began attending summer camps with his father, Brian, a high school football coach himself. He started to create videos and post on social media. The recognition finally came.

Nick Sheridan, then the co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, and JaMarcus Shephard, a former Alabama assistant now coaching at Oregon State, first visited Duncanville to watch Russell throw his junior season. They reported back something that DeBoer still remembers.

"This kid," they said, "is the real deal."

Russell was committed to SMU before DeBoer called him one day to ask if he could slip out of class.

The coach wanted to wish him a happy birthday — and offer him a scholarship to Alabama. He visited, flipped his commitment and the Tide never recruited another quarterback that cycle.

"When you get a call from Alabama, you have to take the call," Russell said.

But there's an alternate path where none of this actually happens.

Russell is humble enough that he actually wanted to transfer away from the glamorous quarterback position. He told his high school head coach, Reginald Samples, that he should move to receiver.

Everyone's quite excited about Keelon back home in the Dallas area.

During a call this week, Tabatha Johnson, his second-grade teacher, excitedly offers a reminder to a reporter that, "I've never been on a phone interview!" Johnson remembers Keelon leading the other second-graders outside for recess where he proceeded to take over as quarterback in a playground football game.

In fact, Russell returned this past May for the school's field day. Johnson still has videos on her phone of him helping teach the kids how to succeed at tug-o-war.

"It's not bulls*** or fake," says Peterman. "He cares about other people."

He's close to his family. In fact, his mother lives in Tuscaloosa, moving there with her son last year. Keelon describes this as a "headache," perhaps only half joking.

"My mom is my best friend," he acknowledges.

Kiersten, his twin sister, moved to the city as well.

On June 6, 2025, Tuscaloosa police confirmed the death of Kiersten. Little to no other information was released, except a request that privacy for the family be respected.

In a message posted on social media, Keelon wrote, "Losing a twin sister and daughter is a pain no one could ever imagine."

The two were close, as many twins are. In fact, Peterman says, they often rode to and from school together.

"You pick Keelon up, you had to get her," he said with a chuckle.

She played basketball at Duncanville High and won a state title the same year that her brother did in football. In a previous interview, April glowed about that season. Those at the school called her "the mother of champions."

In June, Keelon held a camp in Frisco that brought together 100 kids as part of the Forever24 Foundation created in Kiersten's honor. In his video with the university's media staff, Keelon didn't discuss Kiersten, but he mentioned the toughness and fortitude necessary to battle adversity as a major college athlete.

"Who are you as a person? What's your breaking point?" he asked aloud. "You got to be the same person every day."

Keelon's parents separated when he was young, something he openly discusses. He's thankful to have had them both in his life, as well as his five other siblings, including a 10-year-old brother Harlem who trains with Frazier at Old School Quarterbacks.

Harlem will, perhaps, be the next Keelon Russell — an unexpected old soul in a world of vanity, money and fame.

"He doesn't have to try to be cool," says Peterman. "He is just cool. He's El Presidente."

articles.title: England international Cole Palmer signs new Chelsea deal until 2034
articles.summary: Attacking midfielder Palmer has become a key figure in Chelsea’s squad since his arrival from Man City in 2023.
articles.body:
Chelsea ‌attacking midfielder Cole Palmer has ⁠signed a ⁠contract extension that will keep him at Stamford Bridge until 2034, the ⁠Premier League club announced on Saturday.

The 24-year-old England international has become a ⁠key figure since joining Chelsea from Manchester City in 2023, scoring 91 goals in 138 appearances across all competitions.

He was ‌part of the squad that won the Club World Cup in 2025 and the 2024-25 UEFA Conference League.

“Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of ⁠confidence so it was ⁠only right to sign,” Palmer said. “Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions.

“I ⁠feel like we win major trophies here consistently.”

Chelsea have ⁠agreed long-term contracts with several first-team players and emerging talent. Forward Joao Pedro recently signed a deal through 2034, and winger ‌Pedro Neto agreed a six-year contract last month.

Chelsea boss Alonso says Palmer is committed to England

Earlier on Friday, Chelsea ⁠manager Xabi ⁠Alonso insisted Palmer ‌remains committed to playing for England after the attacker drew criticism for missing the recent international break due to injury.

Palmer, ⁠left out of England’s World Cup squad this year after a persistent groin injury affected his ⁠form, was called up by Thomas Tuchel for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia.

However, Palmer was forced to pull out of the squad due ‌to a recurrence of the issue, with Tuchel saying the midfielder “misses too many opportunities” to play in an England shirt.

Asked about Tuchel’s comments, Alonso told reporters: “The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit, that he ⁠enjoys his game, that he is ⁠feeling OK.

“Whenever he is not, like in the Brentford game, we could see that he was struggling. He’s committed but he needs ⁠to be fully fit to play. We need him – the club and ⁠the national team,” the Spaniard ⁠added.

“Now he’s fine. He’s been feeling better this week. We use the ‌first two weeks for him to recover. It’s a little bit from the pubalgia (groin injury) he had.”

Chelsea, ‌10th ‌in the Premier League standings, host 17th-placed Bournemouth later on Saturday.

articles.title: Diego Llorente regresa en la lista de Pellegrini ante Osasuna
articles.standfirst: El central madrileño, recuperado de las molestias que le impidieron jugar antes del parón
articles.summary: El central madrileño, recuperado de las molestias que le impidieron jugar antes del parón
articles.body: Este sábado, tras la última sesión de entrenamiento de la semana para su equipo, Manuel Pellegrini, técnico del Betis, ha dado a conocer la lista de convocados para el partido correspondiente a la octava jornada de LaLiga EA Sports que los verdiblancos disputarán mañana desde las 18.30 horas en el Estadio de La Cartuja frente a Osasuna. La principal novedad es el regreso de Diego Llorente. El central madrileño sufrió una fractura de los huesos propios de la nariz en el duelo ante el Real Madrid del pasado mes y, posteriormente, no participó con el equipo por unas molestias musculares. Ya recuperado, entra entre los citados, al igual que Marc Bartra, que fue sustituido ante el Deportivo de la Coruña, pero que ha aprovechado el parón de selecciones para completar un plan individualizado de trabajo y ponerse a punto. Los lesionados Junior Firpo y Aitor Ruibal son las principales ausencias, junto a Iker Losada, que se queda fuera por decisión técnica. Tampoco entra el tercer portero, Manu González, por lo que sólo hay dos guardametas en la lista en esta ocasión. El resto de futbolistas, incluidos los internacionales que jugaron estos días con sus respectivas selecciones, están disponibles para el Ingeniero en este regreso a la competición. Porteros: Álvaro Valles y Diego Conde Defensas: Bellerín, Ortiz, Bartra, Diego Llorente, Natan, Valentín Gómez y Fran García Centrocampistas: Facundo Bernal, Marc Roca, Nelson Deossa, Fornals, Isco, Fidalgo, Lo Celso, Antony, Abde, Morante y Rodrigo Riquelme Delanteros: Cucho Hernández y Troy Parrot

articles.title: Giráldez: “Veremos si continuamos con la inercia que queríamos todos”
articles.standfirst: Al técnico no le convence el parón de dos semanas
articles.summary: Al técnico no le convence el parón de dos semanas
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez espera que su equipo vuelva en buenas condiciones, pese a las bajas. No le convencen los parones de dos semanas y se prepara para el reto de disputar nueve partidos en cuatro semanas. Prefería que no hubiesen parado: “Me gustaría que se hubiese continuado porque estábamos en una motivación, inercia, con una victoria contundente en casa, la primera. Hemos tenido la mala suerte de tener lesiones, tanto en los que se quedaron aquí como jugadores con sus selecciones, que no es lo ideal. Hemos tenido la recuperación de Iago, de Febas, algún jugador al que le ha venido muy bien este tiempo para poder estar disponible. Veremos mañana si continuamos con la inercia que queríamos todos, que es la del partido del Racing de Santander”. No le convence el parón de dos semanas: “Creo que es corto para ser una pretemporada y largo para ser un parón internacional. Adaptándonos todos los entrenadores como podemos y todos los equipos. Con ganas de que llegue la competición. Yo prefiero que sea una semana de parón, no dos o que sea un mes. Como entrenador de club, prefiero un tiempo largo en el que podamos hacer una minipretemporada o que sea un parón más corto que sirva para recuperar y cargar las pilas para volver a competir. Se ha quedado a medias. Si es la nueva realidad, nos tenemos que acostumbrar y cada vez lo aprovecharemos mejor y todo el mundo lo tendrá más claro”. Lesión de Miguel Román: “Creo que tenemos tres muy buenos mediocentros que en estos momentos de la temporada los tenemos en perfecto estado, recuperado Aleix Febas, buenas sesiones de Burcio con el equipo, Ilaix Moriba, que fue el primero en incorporarse de vuelta con la selección y lleva muchas sesiones con nosotros. En el futuro inmediato, los tres nos van a dar muy buen servicio y veremos, a partir de la carga de minutos y de estos tropecientos partidos que tenemos seguidos, cómo vamos recuperando y si necesitamos algún cuarto jugador, que a priori sería Antañón o alguna modificación en el esquema". Nueve partidos en cuatro semanas: “Planificarlo es un buen reto, está en el récord casi. Es muy difícil, lo hemos visto en el parón. Tienes una idea de que vas a recuperar efectivos y al final estamos menos de cómo nos fuimos, menos jugadores disponibles. Tenemos que centrarnos mucho en el partido que tenemos delante, sabiendo que hay perfiles, en el corto plazo, que te pueden encajar más en el partido de dentro de cuatro días o de siete. Mucho más allá de eso es difícil planificar. Hay posiciones en las que vamos más holgados de jugadores y a lo mejor no vemos tanto a medio plazo". Sobre el Elche: “Es un equipo que tiene una muy buena herencia de una manera de jugar, de mostrarse, de ser atrevidos, cambiando permanentemente estructuras. Tiene una línea muy clara durante años de lo que quieren ser; Anselmi le ha dado su toque a muchas situaciones, más a nivel defensivo, de posicionamiento, de variabilidad defensiva. Es un partido muy táctico, muy rico para nosotros, que hemos tenido la suerte de poder preparar”.

articles.title: Rayo-Athletic: ¿Y ahora qué?
articles.standfirst: Los clubes están por una decisión consensuada y hay opción de jugar ya a puerta cerrada
articles.summary: Los clubes están por una decisión consensuada y hay opción de jugar ya a puerta cerrada
articles.body: La suspensión del Rayo-Athletic es transcedente y ahora queda por ver cuándo se reanuda y cómo se hace, porque podría hacerse este domingo a puerta cerrada. Las relaciones entre Rayo y Athletic son buenas y las dos partes están por una decisión consensuada, aunque la determinación dependerá de Liga y RFEF. La decisión de suspender se decretó por recomendación policial, según afirmaron desde el Rayo Vallecano. Ahora tocará pronunciarse a la justicia deportiva, que entre los supuestos de decisión no contemplará la derrota administrativa del club local. Es el segundo encuentro en este arranque de Liga que el Athletic tiene suspendido ya que tampoco pudo jugar en Levante, en ese caso por fuertes lluvias, y el mismo se recuperará el 21 de octubre. La actuación del organismo de justicia deportiva irá muy ligado al acta que está redactando Sánchez Martínez. El Rayo recibirá una multa con absoluta seguridad que irá aparejada a otro tipo de decisiones, como cierre parcial de grada o del estadio completo. La Liga, a través de un comunicado, condenó "este tipo de comportamientos". La expedición del Athletic regresó al hotel en el que había dormido el viernes a la espera del pronunciamiento oficial de Liga y RFEF respecto a la reanudación del encuentro. Lo más probable es que se juegue este domingo a puerta cerrada en Vallecas, si bien no está descartado que por razones de seguridad se lleve a otro estadio de la Comunidad de Madrid.

articles.title: Arsenal v Leeds : How the players rated
articles.summary: How Arsenal and Leeds players rated following their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Arsenal came from behind as the champions beat Leeds United 2-1 at Emirates Stadium.

James Justin scored the opener for Leeds before Riccardo Calafiori levelled with Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to score the winner.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

David Raya: A smart save to stop Jayden Bogle and then an even better one to deny Gudmundsson soon after. The cross for the Leeds goal evaded him though. 6

Ben White: His header set-up Calafiori for the equaliser. Caught offside a couple of times when Arsenal were building good attacks in the first half. The Leeds goal came down his side. 6

Ezri Konsa: Involved with the physical battle against Calvert-Lewin. 6

Gabriel Magalhaes: It was not the usual convincing performance from the Arsenal back four or Gabriel. 6

Riccardo Calafiori: Scored the equaliser after Arsenal went behind. Tried to make things happen with his adventurous runs but the Arsenal attack did not click. 7

Declan Rice: Tried to inject some energy into the Arsenal as they struggled to create in the first half. A clever assist for Bruno Guimaraes winner. 7

Myles Lewis-Skelly: Back in the Arsenal starting line-up after being dropped for Bruno Guimaraes. Not his best day. 6

Martin Odegaard: Tried to get on the ball to make things happen and had a tame effort saved by Trafford. 6

Bukayo Saka: The winger caused Gudmundsson some problems early but never capitalised on the opportunities. Missed a big late chance to add a third. 6

Noni Madueke: Given the chance to start on the left wing in place of the injured Christos Tzolis. Some good deliveries but not enough of a threat throughout the game. 6

Kai Havertz: Included from the start after picking up a hamstring injury on international duty. Did not look at full match sharpness. 6

Viktor Gyokeres (on 63, Havertz): Brought physicality to the attack. 6

Bruno Guimaraes (on 63, Lewis-Skelly): Came on, changed the game and scored the winner. 8

Jurrien Timber (on 63, White): A calming presence in the backline. 7

Piero Hincapie (on 82, Calafiori): Brought on to see out the win. 6

Merino (on 90, Odegaard): No time to impact. 5

Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, Zubimendi, Eze, Dowman.

James Trafford: Will be disappointed with how he conceded the Arsenal equaliser. Showed his passing range as he tried to pick out target man Dominic Calvert-Lewin. 6

Jayden Bogle: Forced Raya into a save with a good half chance in the first half. Provided an attacking outlet and defended well. 6

James Justin: Scored the very well-worked opener. Made a couple of important clearances and worked well with Bogle in both attack and defence. 7

Tarik Muharemovic: The imposing centre-back dealt with most things that came his way. 7

Nico Elvedi: Part of a Leeds backline that almost caused an upset. 6

Gabriel Gudmundsson: Provided an excellent assist for Justin's goal. Had to deal with the threat of Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz who pulled over to Gudmundsson's side too. 7

Ao Tanaka: Very good on the ball and worked hard alongside Ampadu in the middle of the pitch. 7

Ethan Ampadu: Worked very hard in the middle of the pitch with Tanaka and gave Leeds a solid platform to build from. 6

Anton Stach: The midfielder made his physical presence felt in the middle of the pitch. 6

Noah Okafor: Went close in the first half with an early Leeds chance. Overhit a pass when he had a great chance to play Stach through. 6

Calvert-Lewin: Held the ball up very well and gave Konsa and Gabriel a physical battle. 6

Harry Wilson (on 71, Tanaka): Came on as Leeds chased a way back into the match. 6

Brenden Aaronson (on 71, Okafor): Tried to make something happen. 6

Jean-Matteo Bahoya (on 86, Bogle): Not given many minutes. 5

Jaka Bijol (on 86, Elvedi): Not much time to make an impact. 5

Subs not used: Zetterer, Bard, Gruev, Nmecha, Longstaff.

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Alabama vs. Georgia Weather Forecast, Latest Updates, Game Status amid Hurricane Isaias
articles.summary: While some rain showers are possible, it appears as though Saturday night's SEC football clash between No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, will be largely unencumbered by Hurricane Isaias.
articles.body:
While some rain showers are possible, it appears as though Saturday night's SEC football clash between No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, will be largely unencumbered by Hurricane Isaias.

According to The Weather Channel , Saturday's forecast in Tuscaloosa shows some possible rain with limited wind gusts during the time the game is scheduled to be played.

Georgia vs. Alabama is set for a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff, and the forecast projects a 32 percent chance of rain at 7 p.m. and 31 percent chance at 8 p.m., which drops to 24 percent by 9 p.m.

Also, winds are forecasted to range from about 5 mph to 8 mph, so quarterbacks, kickers and punters shouldn't be impacted significantly.

Per The Weather Channel , Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 hurricane in Destin, Florida, on Friday night.

The storm has left nearly 900,000 people across Florida, Alabama and Georgia without power, and two deaths have been reported.

Despite the dangers of Hurricane Isaias in certain areas, meteorologist Rob Shackelford of The Weather Channel explained why Alabama vs. Georgia will be able to move forward without much issue.

Per Shackelford, Isaias hit a jet stream, which caused some destabilization and resulted in less intense winds.

That is good news for college football fans who are anticipating what could be one of the best games of the 2026 season.

It is always a big deal when Georgia and Alabama meet, and it is especially significant this year given where both teams currently stand.

The Bulldogs and Crimson Tide have matching 5-0 overall and 3-0 SEC records, tying them atop the conference.

Whoever wins Saturday's game will have a big leg up on the other in terms of advancing to the SEC Championship Game and playing for an automatic spot in the College Football Playoff.

However, given the talent level of both teams, it won't be a shock if Saturday is the first of two or even three meetings between them this season.

articles.title: Arsenal 2-1 Leeds: Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes on target as champions fight back to go level with Man City
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Arsenal came from behind to beat Leeds 2-1; James Justin gave the Whites a deserved lead as Daniel Farke's side dominated the opening hour; Riccardo Calafiori levelled seven minutes later, before Bruno Guimaraes came off the bench to snatch the winner
articles.body:
After their 3-0 loss to Brighton before the international break, a blip threatened to become a bigger issue as Leeds not only were the better team for the best part of an hour at the Emirates - but they took the lead through James Justin's strike 10 minutes after half-time.

It was the least Leeds deserved. David Raya made four saves to deny the Whites before the opener - and with Farke's side holding the joint-best defensive record coming into the game, Arsenal were in trouble.

But they were given a lifeline by Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford. The England international, given a chance by Thomas Tuchel during the latest England camp, failed to keep out Riccardo Calafiori's effort from inside the box seven minutes after Leeds' opener.

Mikel Arteta, perhaps unimpressed by his side's performance so far, was unmoved on the touchline - and backed up the leveller with a triple substitution he was planning to make anyway. One of those changes was Bruno Guimaraes, who completed the comeback five minutes later.

Martin Odegaard's ball forward was brilliantly flicked by Declan Rice into the path of the Brazilian on the edge of the box and he crashed the ball into the bottom corner.

Eventually, it rounded off a good week for Arteta, who earlier signed a new deal until 2030.

He made the brave call to play Noni Madueke at left wing over Eberechi Eze to replace the injured Christos Tzolis - and he was Arsenal's best player and was crucial in Calafiori's equaliser. Then the Arsenal made the super sub change for Guimaraes.

Arsenal move level on points with leaders Manchester City at the top of the Premier League, with Enzo Maresca's side facing Liverpool at Anfield on Super Sunday, live on Sky Sports. Leeds, meanwhile, are beaten for the first time in the Premier League this season.

8: CLOSE! Noah Okafor has an early sight of goal as a corner is cleared to his path but his effort is deflected just wide of the far post.

21: BIG CHANCE MISSED! Madueke does well down the left wing and hangs a cross for Havertz, whose header is straight at Trafford.

25: BLOCK! Anton Stach gets a free shot of goal unmarked at the far post but his effort inside the box is blocked by his own team-mate Bogle!

52: WIDE! Justin gets the ball on the edge of the Arsenal box and curls just wide of the far corner.

53: END TO END! Raya makes his fourth save of the game, tipping Ao Tanaka's long-range drive over the bar.

55: GOAL! Leeds make the pressure count as Gudmundsson's cross flies across goal and Justin crashes the ball into the net at the back post.

62: GOAL! Madueke's cross is put across the penalty area by Ben White, leaving Calafiori to tap home.

70: GOAL! Five minutes after coming on, Guimaraes slams Arsenal in front after being teed up by Rice's flick.

"We knew it was going to be really tough, we are coming from three weeks without 16 players [because of internationals] after a heavy defeat [against Brighton] and we had all these things in the tummy.

"Today we had two objectives, one face the challenge because this is a team that hasn't lost in the Premier League and they are in a great position because they fully deserved it. And secondly because we had a point to prove something was touched in our identity against Brighton, especially in the manner that we reacted after being in a difficult situation and context.

"And today even though we started extremely well and being really dominant we didn't capitalise on the spaces, the situation, the overloads that we had to attack the goal and the box. So that left the game a little bit open and we knew that they don't need much to threaten you.

"Every time they are putting the ball in the box, they are incredibly dangerous and we got into a situation with losing 1-0, at home after a defeat, 12.30pm kick-off, it is a bad mixture. And we got out of that through pinching our desire to win, to have a reaction to show the personality and courage that we have in this team.

"And once the equaliser went in, the energy changed, the finishers came in and made a huge difference again to help us to win the game and that's what we are made of.

"And we know that it's going to be every single week the same, because every game that I have watched in those three weeks [during the international break], it's not going to be any different to that."

Farke: We deserved more - but it's Arsenal

"It's difficult to describe the emotions. Congratulations to Arsenal. It's down to their mentality Mikel has created here that even on a tough day they found a way to win.

"My emotions are mixed. Heartbroken and gutted for my players because they deserved to travel back with points today. After such a good away performance to travel back without any points is tough.

"I am very proud of what was a top away performance. First half was on a really good level, we did not allow any chances. We looked more dangerous.

"And I told them at half-time, if we have a bit more clarity and belief in our offensive actions we will win this game. We fully deserved to go and lead.

"But it's Arsenal, it is one of the best teams in Europe, certainly the most consistent. This means they are one of the best teams in the world."

Madueke shines in new-ish position for Arsenal

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at the Emirates Stadium:

Noni Madueke can be a frustrating player to watch at times. Arsenal and Chelsea fans have seen it. England fans witnessed it at the World Cup. Even Mikel Arteta feels it.

"When I haven't liked so much what he was doing or it wasn't impacting the game, I made certain decisions, he has accepted them," the Arsenal manager said.

But this was a display where Madueke shone - and led the way - in a slightly different role.

Madueke lined up on the left wing for Arsenal against Leeds. He has only started two games for the Gunners in that position - the first came 14 months ago in the 5-0 win over Leeds. That was his full Arsenal debut.

But with Christos Tzolis injured, Arsenal have been a bit short at left wing. Many expected Eberechi Eze to fill in - but Madueke got the nod and as Arteta said: "He took his chance."

Madueke was Arsenal's best forward player on the day, creating three chances - that Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard should have put away.

He then played a big role in the equaliser, with his right-footed cross finding Ben White at the back post, who then set up Riccardo Calafiori.

Madueke was the only Arsenal player to complete a cross against Leeds - and he completed five crosses from six attempts. He was making things happen - he has been doing it for a while in front of Arteta.

"What he's done is raise the level. And in training he's been the best player in the last 10 days. You could see that every time he was in and around the ball he looked a threat."

Like other signings last season, including Viktor Gyokeres and Martin Zubimendi, Madueke's Arsenal career was at risk of stalling. Has he now found a second wind in a new position?

articles.title: Swansea City 2-1 Norwich City: Moussa Yeo, Adam Idah score as Swans extend lead at Championship summit
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Swansea City and Norwich City at the Swansea.com Stadium on Saturday; Moussa Kounfolo Yeo and Adam Idah cancel out Jacob Wright's opener to extend the Swans' lead at the top of the table
articles.body:
The Republic of Ireland striker came back to haunt his first club with a glancing header in the 59th minute to complete his side's comeback after falling behind to Jacob Wright's goal in the first half.

Swansea emerged from the international break with an injury to Canadian Stephen Eustaquio. He joined Josh Key on the injury list, while the Canaries were without top scorer Mohamed Toure.

West Ham's draw the night before left the Swans sitting pretty at the top of the table as they sought to extend their unbeaten home run in the Championship to five. They looked a little rusty and Norwich harassed and hounded them on the ball to knock them out of shape.

It took 15 minutes before Moussa Yeo unleashed the first shot of the game from just outside the Norwich box but Vladan Kovacevic saved comfortably. Moments later Mathias Kvistgaarden had a chance at the other end after Pelle Mattsson put him in a good position to shoot.

Joseph Opoku gave top scorer Idah a great chance to add to his three goals already this season in the 22nd minute after winning the ball on halfway and driving to the Norwich box. Idah took a heavy touch from what looked to be a scoring pass and Kovacevic saved.

Norwich were quick on the counter-attack and a great cross from the left forced Stephen Welsh to head over from under the Swansea bar to concede a corner.

The corner was cleared but Andre Brooks and Oscar Schwartau combined to rob Welsh of the ball and Schwartau passed across the box to enable Wright to score in the 28th minute.

Idah had two more chances to level matters before the break, but again Kovacevic was up to the mark to deny him.

It took the league leaders a mere four minutes after the restart to get back on level terms when Yeo made it three goals in as many games. Some neat interplay on the left touchline eventually freed Josh Tymon and his cross was missed at the near post by Idah before being converted at the back post by Yeo.

Swansea looked a different side in the second half and Goncalo Franco set up Idah for a shot that Kovacevic saved, then Ruairi McConville cleared off the line as Opoku fired the rebound goalwards.

The second goal came just before the hour as Idah headed home from an inch-perfect cross from Melker Widell. Moments later Idah limped off to be replaced by Zan Vipotnik.

Norwich had two good chances in the dying minutes but Lawrence Vigouroux saved Sam Field's shot and then saw Jovon Makama head over the bar from five yards out.

"We started well but lacked a little bit of precision in the first half in some situations. It was something that we could easily improve.

"Then we suffered, bounced back quite well and improved a lot in the second half in terms of rhythm and intensity. I'm really happy with the boys and it was really important for us to win more than anything.

"Players had been flying around because of the international break, joining on the last days of training as well before the game. It's not the easiest way to prepare, not only for us but of course for a lot of teams in the league.

"It's always important to get results after an international break, and this was quite a long one. I wasn't concerned about us losing momentum, I was more concerned in terms of the quality of our game.

"The players have come back to play three games in eight days, so there's not a lot of time to train. It's all about trying to reconnect everyone."

"It was frustrating not to get at least a point out of the game. I thought the first half we were in control and one team wasn't better than the other.

"We scored a really good goal from a collective attack and that was a good way to go into half-time. You could feel that their fans were getting nervous at the end of the first half because they were not creating many chances, which they normally do.

"In some moments we should have won more duels and maybe some players came out thinking too much about the result and freezing a bit. We didn't have the same intensity as in the first half.

"That's why I made changes after we went 2-1 down. In the last half-hour we stepped up again and we had two really good chances to make it 2-2.

"We were much better organised than in the Bolton game last time out and we need to keep building from here. If we keep on pushing, keep on growing in confidence, then the results will come."

articles.title: Rayo-Athletic: La Liga comunica que el partido no se reanudará el domingo
articles.standfirst: Los dos clubes estaban de acuerdo en que el encuentro se jugase de inmediato
articles.summary: Los dos clubes estaban de acuerdo en que el encuentro se jugase de inmediato
articles.body: El Rayo-Athletic no se reanudará este domingo porque la Liga ha comunicado a los clubes que "el partido suspendido no se podrá jugar ni a lo largo del día de hoy ni de mañana domingo". Las dos entidades estaban por jugarlo de inmediato, pero no se han dado las condiciones para que la Liga lo pudiese ratificar. Cerca de las 16.30 horas Raúl Martín Presa, máxima autoridad del Rayo y la diana de las críticas de la afición, ha abandonado el estadio con la comunicación oficial acerca de la no reanudación rápida del encuentro. Los jugadores y técnicos del Athletic esperaban en su hotel de concentración la decisión del organismo y al conocer que no había posibilidad de jugarse mañana la expedición ha tomado camino de regreso a Bilbao. La intención inicial que manejaban los clubes era jugar el partido ya, probablemente a puerta cerrada, pero había que poner de acuerdo tanto a las instituciones deportivas como a los responsables de seguridad. Y no ha habido opcion. El aplazamiento sine die del encuentro complica el calendario de los dos equipos, pero sobre todo el del Athletic, que ya tiene retrasado un partido con el Levante. Los leones recuperarán el primero de esos partidos el 21 de octubre en el Ciutat de Valencia, que es una semana de competiciones europeas. El proceder que se seguirá para acomodar el Rayo-Athletic, salvo que se proponga jugar el martes o miércoles de esta misma semana, será similar al empleado para fijar el Levante-Athletic y se jugará también en fecha europea. Los siguientes miércoles de semana continental antes del parón navideño serán 4 de noviembre, 25 de noviembre y 9 de diciembre. La Liga y la RFEF no han establecido todavía las condiciones para la disputa del encuentro, pero todo apunta a que será a puerta cerrada.

articles.title: La Liga match abandoned as Rayo Vallecano fans throw paper planes onto pitch
articles.summary: Rayo Vallecano's match against Athletic Club was abandoned after the home fans threw paper airplanes onto the pitch in protest against the club's owner.
articles.body:
Rayo Vallecano's match against Athletic Club was abandoned on Saturday after the home fans threw paper planes and rubber balls on to the pitch in protest against the club's owner.

The La Liga game was Rayo's first of the season at the Estadio de Vallecas, which had been temporarily closed after an audit highlighted serious health and safety issues - including a risk of contracting Legionnaires' disease .

Rayo fans blame owner and president Raul Martin Presa, who has long been criticised for the poor upkeep of facilities and a failure to modernise the club.

In the 13th minute of the game, when Rayo fans usually chant "Presa leave now", supporters threw paper planes and small rubber balls on to the pitch.

The referee stopped play and the stadium announcer urged fans not to throw objects on to the pitch, while stewards hastily removed the items from the grass.

When play resumed 15 minutes later, supporters in the south stand again threw objects on to the field and the referee abandoned play with the game goalless.

Following the game, Athletic Club released a statement to say they would contact their fans who travelled to the game in Madrid to arrange refunds.

Last season, the Spanish football association published a letter written by Rayo's players that described the Vallecas pitch as "unplayable" and noted a lack of hot water in the showers and inadequate cleaning.

They began last season without being able to use their own training ground because of mould. However, they were able to reach the final of the Uefa Conference League, which they lost 1-0 to Crystal Palace.

Supporters regularly have to queue for hours to purchase match tickets at the stadium's small box office as Rayo is the only top-flight Spanish club without a ticketing website.

Rayo sit 13th in La Liga with two wins from their opening seven games.

articles.title: El Bayern amortigua la 'pifia' que dejará señalado a Neuer de por vida
articles.standfirst: El veterano guardameta alemán encajó el gol más rápido en la historia de la Bundesliga en el empate contra el Augsburgo (2-2)
articles.summary: El veterano guardameta alemán encajó el gol más rápido en la historia de la Bundesliga en el empate contra el Augsburgo (2-2)
articles.body: Manuel Neuer siempre será recordado como uno de los mejores porteros de la historia... a pesar de haber cometido alguna que otra 'pifia' sonada. La de esta tarde, sin embargo, le dejará señalado de por vida... a la par que alimentará el debate sobre su titularidad por delante de Urbig. El Bayern, al menos, logró amortiguarlo rescatando un empate a domicilio en el derbi regional ante el Augsburgo (2-2). La presencia de Saibari como mediapunta junto a Olise y Luis Díaz fue la única novedad que introdujo Kompany para paliar la lesión sufrida por Musiala durante el parón de selecciones con Alemania. Ambos laterales, posición más abierta en este Bayern, fueron ocupados por Stanisic y Davies. Apenas seis segundos. Eso es lo que tardó el Augsburgo en firmar el gol más rápido en la historia de la Bundesliga... superando al de Bellarabi con el Leverkusen allá por agosto de 2014. Todo se originó desde el saque de centro a cargo de Luis Díaz jugando atrás sobre Neuer: el control se le fue largo, trató de sortear la presión de Fellhauer 'picándole' el balón... y éste le acabó robando la cartera. El encuentro no podía haber arrancado de peor manera para un Bayern Múnich que, en ningún momento, logró imprimirle el habitual ritmo vertiginoso a sus ataques... mientras que el Augsburgo, sobre todo a través de Ribeiro, estaba logrando amenazar en transición. Juma Bah, que debutaba, llegó a perdonar el 0-2 a la salida de un córner en el 35'. No es habitual ver a un Bayern tan desconectado. Olise no lograba superar a Behrens y Luis Díaz estaba completamente apagado. No fue hasta el descuento cuando, de verdad, comenzaron a apretar. Saibari, blando a las manos de Dahmen, se apuntó el primer remate a puerta y, en la última acción, Kane mandó al larguero un centro lateral de Pavlovic. No intervino Kompany al descanso con la idea de que el Bayern diese continuidad a la rebeldía mostrada en el tramo final del primer acto. La suerte, eso sí, tampoco parecía de su lado con el gol anulado a Luis Díaz por un fuera de juego previo de Stanisic. Menos de cinco minutos más tarde, sin embargo, Kane habilitó la ruptura de Saibari a su espalda para igualar el choque. Se esperaba un 'vendaval' por parte del Bayern. Ahora bien, escasos 10' después, el Augsburgo volvió a hacer saltar la sorpresa. Salieron con metros aprovechando un latifundio en la medular, Neuer estuvo lento a la hora de lanzarse para orientar su despeje a disparo de Brackelmann y Rodrigo Ribeiro culminó su excelente actuación recogiendo el rechace. Kompany, de inmediato, dio entrada a 'Nene' Brown como lateral derecho a pie cambiado y a Gnabry por un Saibari que parecía más entonado que Olise o Luis Díaz. En cuestión de cinco minutos, ambos a pase de Kane, le anularon dos goles al Bayern. El inglés, sin embargo, apareció en el 80' para tirar una pared con Pavlovic y regalarle el 2-2 al propio Brown. Gnabry, nada más reanudarse el juego, mandó un balón al palo desde el área pequeña libre de marca. Acabó pidiendo la hora un Augsburgo que fue el único equipo capaz de tumbarles el curso pasado en Bundesliga. El Bayern salvó el invicto... pero no aprovechó el 'pinchazo' del Dortmund para situarse líderes.

articles.title: Mastantuono no puede evitar un nuevo batacazo de la Fiorentina
articles.standfirst: La derrota deja a los 'violas' antepenúltimos con cuatro puntos de 18 posibles
articles.summary: La derrota deja a los 'violas' antepenúltimos con cuatro puntos de 18 posibles
articles.body: La Fiorentina no consigue coger 'velocidad de crucero'. Se marchó al 'parón' después de empatar con el Nápoles (1-1) y de golear al Venezia (2-4) con un 'hat-trick' de Franco Mastantuono... pero ha regresado con un tropiezo ante el Genoa (2-1). Los del recién regresado Paolo Vanoli, que alineó de inicio a De Gea, Álex Jiménez, Valdepeñas y Mastantuono, ya perdían en el 7'. De Gea desvió un disparo desde la frontal, pero nada pudo hacer cuando el excadista Milutin Osmajic le fusiló a placer tras un remate en semifallo de Mikael Egill. En el 15' llegó el 2-0, nuevamente con Osmajic como protagonista. El ex del Cádiz ganó la espalda a la defensa y sirvió el pase de la muerte para que Junior Messias marcara a placer. Pudo recortar distancias la Fiorentina en el 19'. Bloqueó la defensa un disparo de Mastantuono en la frontal... pero Gnonto estaba en fuera de juego cuando recogió el rechace. Rozó el 2-1 el propio Mastantuono en el 45'. Lo hizo con un disparo marca de la casa. Buscó el palo largo desde el costado derecho del área. Sin embargo, se topó con una gran intervención de Biljow para desviar el balón. Los 'viola' recortaron distancias, definitivamente, en el 72'. Abrió a la derecha Cher Ndour y Johan Vásquez terminó desviando el centrochut del español Álex Jiménez contra su propia portería. No pudo ser. La Fiorentina necesita mejorar. La derrota le deja antepenúltima con cuatro puntos, uno por debajo del Genoa, que también tiene cuatro puntos.

articles.title: Arsenal 2-1 Leeds: A decisive moment of real quality - but Mikel Arteta still has issues to address
articles.summary: Heroics and battling performances have already become a theme of Arsenal's season with Bruno Guimaraes coming to the rescue again.
articles.body:
For the second time in three Premier League matches, Bruno Guimaraes has come to Arsenal 's rescue.

Having sparked their 2-0 win at Sunderland in September with the crucial first goal, the £75m summer signing came off the bench again to have a pivotal impact against Leeds on Saturday.

This time it was the winner as the Gunners came from behind for a 2-1 success in a testing encounter at Emirates Stadium.

But Ecuador international Piero Hincapie was carried off during the warm-down, raising concern the defender has suffered an injury.

He came on as a late substitute against Daniel Farke's side but completed extra running after the final whistle - a practice most clubs use.

A fifth win in six league games put Mikel Arteta's side level on points with leaders Manchester City , but their title defence has certainly not been without its scares so far.

Following on from their comprehensive 3-0 defeat at Brighton last time out, Arsenal fell behind in a league match for a third time in four league matches - and only a David Raya penalty save stopped them from trailing at Sunderland as well.

For large parts of the game against Leeds , they were nowhere near their best but, after going behind in the 55th minute, Riccardo Calafiori and Guimaraes - on his full home debut - secured an important three points.

"It was a great game of football. Leeds were brilliant for one hour." said Ally McCoist on TNT Sports.

"Mikel Arteta made changes when he needed to and the substitutions gave Arsenal what they needed. That's what champions do. Leeds can hold their heads high."

By getting wins when below par the mark of champions or are there reasons for concern for Arteta and Arsenal ?

Guimaraes raises level after Brighton woe

Coming into the season as defending champions, Arsenal were looking to make a statement signing to make their rivals take notice.

They did not bring in the attacker they wanted but Guimaraes looks like he could be that key arrival to help Arteta's men build on their success.

The 28-year-old midfielder is a 'win-now' signing in the peak years of his career.

He responded well to a disappointing performance in the defeat by Brighton , where he made his full league debut.

The Brazilian international has now scored two goals that have helped his side to valuable points and justified the decision to spend big on Guimaraes, even if the Gunners are inundated with top quality options in midfield.

Arteta said: "He wasn't at that level against Brighton , and this is the level for Arsenal . Every week, every game, every minute, every action, you have to be at that level.

"Today was much better. That's what we have to demand, and this is what I demand to myself. I'm going to demand the same with the players, because if we do that, he will raise the standards and we will be a better team."

Guimaraes was the first player to score twice from the bench this season and both goals have been from outside the box.

'The last time we put our shirts on, something was missing'

Arsenal won the league last season in part because of their excellent defence.

The Gunners conceded the fewest goals in the league but have already conceded five in six games.

The partnership of Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba is one of the best in the world and Arsenal look to be missing the injured Frenchman's calmness.

Ezri Konsa was brought in from Aston Villa for £55m and, despite his quality, is still getting used to his new surroundings.

It is unclear how serious Hincapie's injury is, although he was seen clutching his right ankle as he was carried off by goalkeeper Illan Meslier.

He signed for the club on a permanent deal this summer, having initially joined on loan from Bayer Leverkusen last season.

Hincapie has suffered from muscular issues this term and now faces an anxious wait to discover whether he requires another spell on the sidelines.

Left-back Calafiori, though, has proved integral to Arsenal 's attacking threat. His equaliser against Leeds was his first league strike this term but no defender has been involved in more Premier League goals than the Italian (one goal, two assists).

"The last time we put our shirts on, something was missing." added Arteta.

"And we need to be very conscious of that. From being exceptional and being the champions to being extremely average, like in that game, is a really thin line.

"So if you don't want it more than the opponent, you are not able to cope emotionally with certain situations, you're going to suffer.

"And we all suffered and we didn't enjoy that game, but then you have to learn the lesson and we certainly done that.

"We speak about it and you could sense that there was something in those tummies."

Madueke gets chance after attacking struggles

Arteta made some big calls when naming his starting XI.

He opted to start with German Kai Havertz up front despite the forward returning early from international duty after picking up a hamstring issue, leaving Viktor Gyokeres on the bench again.

Gyokeres had scored four goals, registering in every match for Sweden, in the last international break, but looks to have work to do to win his manager round.

The 28-year-old has yet to start a Premier League game and in his cameos this season has looked far from the level required as a striker who could fire Arsenal to back-to-back titles.

The forward line did not click against Leeds and, with Havertz looking like he lacked match sharpness, thoughts turned towards whether Arsenal missing out on an elite attacker in the summer would haunt them.

Winger Christos Tzolis, who has shone at times this season following his summer arrival, suffered a hamstring issue with Greece and, with Eberechi Eze out of form, Arteta used Noni Madueke on the left wing.

Madueke was left out of the last England squad due to a lack of minutes with Arsenal but, after "being the best player in training for the last 10 days" according to Arteta, now could be the chance for him to prove his worth.

articles.title: Manita del 'Xabi Alonso Express' con dobletes de Joao Pedro y Henderson y la primera asistencia de Chavarría
articles.standfirst: Los 'blues' ya ganaban 2-0 a los 129 segundos de partido
articles.summary: Los 'blues' ya ganaban 2-0 a los 129 segundos de partido
articles.body: Confesaba Xabi Alonso que le gustaba más el anterior parón de selecciones, más corto. A 'su' Chelsea, sin embargo, le sentó bien. 'Amaneció' con la noticia de la renovación de Cole Palmer hasta 2034... y a los 149 segundos ya ganaba 2-0, con Pep Chavarría de titular, un partido que terminó con 'manita' sobre el Bournemouth (5-1). Abrió la cuenta el veterano Jordan Henderson en el 2'. Condujo Palmer y marcó el internacional inglés, de 36 años, con un disparo al palo largo que tocó en el poste antes de entrar. El 2-0 llegó en el 3'. Abrió el propio Henderson a la derecha y Morgan Rogers conectó un disparo que António Silva terminó desviando contra su propia portería. Se le dan bien los inicios a la 'Xabineta': seis de los 15 goles que lleva en Premier han llegado en los primeros 10'. A los 'blues', sin embargo, les gusta complicarse. 'El Dibu' Martínez salvó un mano a mano con Truffert en el 36' y un cabezazo de António Silva en el añadido. Regresó del descanso el Chelsea y volvió a marcar en el primer minuto. Pedro Neto le robó la cartera a António Silva y cedió para que Joao Pedro marcara en boca de gol. La asignatura pendiente del Chelsea, en cualquier caso, sigue siendo dejar la portería a cero. Un córner mal defendido acabó en un mal despeje de Moisés Caicedo que taponó Evanilson para enviar el balón a la red en el 51'. En el 67' llegó la primera asistencia de Pep Chavarría con el Chelsea. Dobló a Morgan Rogers y sirvió un gran centro a la espalda de la defensa para que Joao Pedro firmara su doblete. Faltaba aún el mejor gol del partido. Lo marcó Jordan Henderson para redondear la 'manita' en el 70'. El ex de Sunderland, Liverpool, Ajax, Ettifaq y Brentford transformó un gran gol de falta desde 30 metros. El triunfo sitúa al Chelsea, provisionalmente, quinto, con 10 puntos de 18 posibles. El Bournemouth, sin Iraola, es cuarto por la cola con tres puntos.

articles.title: El Aston Villa de Emery no despega
articles.standfirst: Los 'villanos' sólo suman una victoria en seis jornadas
articles.summary: Los 'villanos' sólo suman una victoria en seis jornadas
articles.body: El Aston Villa, incapaz de resguardar la ventaja obtenida tras su remontada, no ha pasado del empate en Birmingham ante el Brentford (2-2) y sigue anclado en la parte baja de la clasificación, con una sola victoria en seis partidos. El conjunto de Emery, que logró ganar por primera vez antes del parón internacional, al Tottenham, colista (2-3), no pudo dar continuidad a ese buen marcador y se topó con el cuadro de Keith Andrews, instalado en la zona alta y todavía invicto. De hecho, el Brentford tomó ventaja a los diez minutos con un gol del ucraniano Yegor Yarmolyuk después de una buena jugada por la izquierda de Igor Thiago y un despeje de Victor Lindelof. Respondió a los dos minutos el equipo local con un tanto de Nicolas Jackson, que aprovechó un tiro en semifallo de Emiliano Buendía, convertido en asistencia, después de un pase de John McGinn. El propio McGinn fue el que puso por delante al Aston Villa a falta de un cuarto de hora para el final cuando batió por segunda vez a Caoimhin Kelleher con un disparo dentro del área, asistido por Johan Manzambi. Pero el Brentford evitó que el cuadro de Emery asimilara la ventaja y dos minutos más tarde, Kristoffer Ajer, en una acción individual, estableció la igualada final que deja a los visitantes en el cuarto lugar y al Villa decimocuarto, lejos de su objetivo.

articles.title: Nick Saban Praises Jalen Hurts' Character After Viral Video of Benching in CFP Title Game
articles.summary: Former Alabama coach Nick Saban circled back on his famous decision to bench Jalen Hurts at halftime of the 2018 national title game.
articles.body:
Former Alabama coach Nick Saban circled back on his famous decision to bench Jalen Hurts at halftime of the 2018 national title game.

ESPN's new docuseries on Saban included footage from inside the locker room as he made the switch:

Appearing on College GameDay , the retired coach called it "one of the most difficult decisions I ever had to make as a coach." He praised Hurts for how he "managed and handled the adversity and the difficult circumstance that he was put in."

"This guy's character in that situation has been understated," Saban said. "And I think people should recognize how much character he really has, and that's what has propelled him to be a great player in the NFL and [win] a Super Bowl."

Saban's gambit paid off handsomely. With Tua Tagovailoa at the helm, Alabama scored 20 points in the second half against SEC rival Georgia. Tagovailoa won the game in overtime when he hit DeVonta Smith with a 41-yard touchdown pass.

The writing was on the wall as to who would be the starting quarterback for the 2018 season. Despite the fact he'd be relegated to backup status, Hurts stuck around.

In an appropriate twist of fate, he replaced an injured Tagovailoa in the SEC championship and guided the offense on pair of fourth-quarter scoring drives in a 35-28 victory over Georgia.

Few would've blamed Hurts for exiting — he transferred to Oklahoma for his final year in 2019 — in the wake of the 2018 title game. Saban made the right decision, but it was a harsh assessment of a QB who had started 29 games for him over two years.

Things worked out nicely for Hurts in the end. He was the Heisman Trophy runner-up with the Sooners and continued to defy his skeptics with the Philadelphia Eagles in the NFL.

What unfolded inside the Tide locker room in Atlanta may have been a blessing in disguise.

articles.title: Dundee United 1-0 Hibs: Daniel Bennie gets Dundee United winner as Marink Reedijk loses first game in charge
articles.summary: Report as Daniel Bennie scores the only goal of the game to hand Marink Reedijk defeat in his first match as Hibernian boss
articles.body:
The hosts scored the only goal of the game in the first half through on-loan QPR winger Daniel Bennie to secure the Terrors a first home league win of the season as the visitors finished the game with 10 men after sub Jacob Devaney was sent off.

The result moves United up to fifth in the Premiership table while Hibs remain in 10th place.

Hibs had the first opportunity of the game in the ninth minute when the ball was played to Felix Passlack with the defender finding Josh Mulligan but the midfielder's shot was blocked.

United responded with Lyall Cameron playing in Jesse Randall but his shot was straight at Hibs goalie Raphael Sallinger who stood tall to block.

The same two home players combined well again in the 23rd minute and this time Sallinger had to produce a stunning stop to send Randall's shot over the bar.

The Terrors were well on top and should have opened the scoring when Bennie was presented with a great chance inside the box but he sent his curling effort over the bar.

Bennie, though, made no mistake in the 35th minute when Cameron dinked a cross to him and he bundled home from close range.

After the break, Sallinger had to rescue Hibs once more to keep out a low Randall shot but the visitors broke straight up the park through sub Rabbi Matondo, with Bert Esselink having to make a vital interception.

United thought they had been awarded a penalty in the 80th minute when Neil Farrugia tumbled after a push by Hibs sub Devaney.

Referee Don Robertson initially pointed to the spot and booked Devaney but, after being called to the monitor by the VAR, he decided the challenge was outside the box and instead gave a free-kick and then brandished a red card at Devaney for a last-man challenge.

Hibs came close to drawing the game in added time but United keeper Jack Walton made a great stop low down from a Boyle shot.

"I felt it was deserved, over the whole piece.

"To follow up the really good performance in Paisley with another good performance and result - two clean sheets and back-to-back wins in the league. That is not an easy thing to do.

"And getting our first league win at home is an important factor as well."

"We just need one moment and we need to believe that one moment will come in order to flip the game around.

"I think and believe that this team is able to do better than what we have seen today and also better than what we have seen over the last few weeks, especially when you're 1-0 down."

articles.title: Hearts 5-0 St Mirren: Laurent Mendy, Calvin Miller, Claudio Braga and Josh McPake all score as Jambos record biggest home win since 2023
articles.summary: Report as Laurent Mendy, Calvin Miller, Claudio Braga and Josh McPake all hit the back of the net as goal-hungry Hearts thrash St Mirren
articles.body:
The third-placed Jambos dominated from the start and rarely looked in any danger from the moment Laurent Mendy fired them ahead in the 20th minute.

Calvin Miller then notched two penalties, either side of half-time, before further goals from Claudio Braga and Josh McPake ensured a smooth afternoon for Wouter Vrancken's side ahead of their Conference League opener at home to Nordsjaelland on Thursday.

It was Hearts' biggest league win at Tynecastle since they defeated Ross County 6-1 under Steven Naismith in April 2023, and they are now comfortably the top scorers in the league. Saints, by contrast, left Edinburgh licking their wounds after a fourth defeat in succession.

Hearts started brightly, with Harry Milne, Miller and McPake - buoyed by making his Scotland debut against Slovenia on Tuesday - all threatening early on.

Saints were offering little, although Killian Phillips tried to catch Beau Reus out with a lob from the centre circle after a misplaced pass from James Wilson.

A minute later Milne went clean through but saw his shot pushed over by Buddies keeper Jacob Chapman.

Hearts made a deserved breakthrough in the 19th minute. Miller floated a free-kick into the box and Mendy got his header all wrong, sending it back the way, but Saints' Chris Mochrie inadvertently knocked it back to the former Forest Green midfielder, who pounced to lash a powerful finish, on the bounce, high past Chapman from 12 yards out.

The visitors were bedraggled, unable to generate any rhythm, and they fell further behind in the 32nd minute. McPake was tripped by Alex Gogic as he burst into the box, and Miller duly sent Chapman the wrong way from the spot.

Having seen his team outplayed in the first half, McLeish made a triple change for the start of the second half. But the first notable involvement of one of those substitutes, Liam Donnelly, was to give away a penalty for tripping Wilson in the box, and Miller stepped up to convert his second spot-kick in the 50th minute.

Miller turned provider four minutes later as his nicely weighted pass released Braga, who rounded Chapman before slotting home despite the efforts of two Saints defenders to get back and clear.

After Reus made a brilliant save to deny Calvin Ramsay, the outstanding McPake got himself clear in the box to fire past the exposed Chapman from eight yards in the 80th minute.

"From the first session (in the summer), the players liked what we were doing and they tried to make those steps and you see it today that they are trying to do it and succeeding.

"We try to play a kind of football that is positive and constructive and proactive, and not a reaction.

"I think people come to the stadium to see nice football, to see goals from your side.

"Also for the players, we try to play a style of football that, when you were a little boy, when you started playing football on the street, you played football to score goals, not to stay in front of your goal and prevent the goals.

"You want to score goals because this is the nicest feeling you have in football.

"We are trying to play a type of football where we can come in the positions as much as possible to get this feeling. Some days it will work better than other days, but it's nice to see that it worked well today.

"It's good for the guys that they have such a game where they felt comfortable on the ball. Also out of possession we were good. Hopefully it gives us more confidence for this run of games."

"It's not good enough from our point of view. We shot ourselves in the foot and gave away two penalties which are avoidable.

"There were individual errors for the other three and that's not to take anything away from Hearts, who were excellent.

"You can't come to places like this and expect to play football from the first minute, you have to earn that right. You have to fight and out-run teams and we didn't do that at points.

"It's not an excuse but we lost Niko Agrafiotis in the warm-up and he's a big part of what we're trying to do. We had to shuffle things around and it didn't quite happen for us.

"We all have to take responsibility. I have to rectify it."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Falkirk 1-2 Dundee: Ashley Hay nets stoppage-time winner as Dundee come from behind to win away from home
articles.summary: Report as Ashley Hay snatches a dramatic victory for Dundee; Owen Bevan was also on target for the away side after Jacob Murrell's first-half penalty for Falkirk
articles.body:
The striker, out since early August with a ligament sprain, converted from close range after latching on to Ethan Hamilton's free-kick in the first minute of added time.

His goal completed the turnaround after Owen Bevan's second goal for the Dark Blues had cancelled out Jacob Murrell's first-half penalty at Falkirk Stadium.

Dundee mustered five attempts on target by the 26th minute and looked dangerous on every forward raid. Lewis Neilson, in for Deniss Melniks in Falkirk's only change from their last outing at St Johnstone in September, blocked a goalbound Bradley Fink volley inside 60 seconds.

Then, after 12 minutes, Drey Wright spied Scott Bain well out of goal and tried to embarrass him from 60 yards. The quickly-taken free-kick was on target and forced Bain to backpedal smartly to tip over the crossbar.

Falkirk had toiled to craft a chance from open play but were gifted the opportunity to lead in the 31st minute.

Finley Barbrook, with his back to goal, went down under a clumsy challenge from Callum Jones and American striker Murrell made no mistake from the penalty spot.

Falkirk settled thereafter and could have been two up by the break when Bain released Leon McCann with a long ball to split the visiting defence - but the full-back was hesitant in going for goal and, once under pressure, his lobbed attempt bounded wide.

Dundee drew level seven minutes into the second period. Joe Bevan did well to keep the ball in play from a corner and Wright clipped a cross back into the danger area where Owen Bevan towered to nod home from six yards.

Fink fired home in the 63rd minute but was swiftly denied by an offside flag rubber-stamped by VAR.

Dundee keeper Owen Goodman was at full stretch to deny both Murrell and Ben Krauhaus.

At the other end, Fink then Joe Bevan offered weak finishes and it looked like a share of the points was in order.

But a stoppage-time set piece swung in by Hamilton hit off Hay who reacted smartly to force home.

In a frantic finish, Goodman touched on to the bar in a goalmouth melee at the other end to preserve the points.

"When you consider the adversity this group has faced, it's an amazing result and achievement.

"It ranks very highly, for me. You're 1-0 down at half-time, and we had Joe Bevan really struggling. Physios said he might only last another 10 minutes. I used the word 'grit' at half-time and reminded him on the pitch.

"We had to show a lot of that to come back in this game.

"It was a very appropriate word for the second half performance.

"It was gritty, determined and guys like Joe are really growing in stature and mindset."

"We should've taken something from it, but we've found a way to lose it.

"We have to show a lot more character and personality.

"If you give away a free-kick, we have to defend it better."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Sunderland 0-2 Brighton: Seagulls stay third in Premier League after third straight league win without conceding
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Brighton win 2-0 at Sunderland; second-half goals from Maxim De Cuyper and substitute Jaouen Hadjam made it three straight Premier League wins without conceding for the visitors, who stay third in the table
articles.body:
Fabian Hurzeler's side backed up their dominant 3-0 home victory over champions Arsenal before the international break with an equally impressive display on Wearside thanks to second-half goals from Maxim De Cuyper and substitute Jaouen Hadjam.

Captain Pascal Gross once again controlled the game from midfield, creating the key opener eight minutes into the second period to become the oldest player to provide an assist in three successive top-flight games - at the age of 35 years and 117 days - since Ryan Giggs in February 2012.

Despite Pascal Struijk being shown a straight red card just before the hour mark - after the VAR Neil Davies decided the centre-back had hauled down Wilson Isidor as the Sunderland striker broke clear on goal - the visitors were rarely troubled thereafter, before sealing the win in stoppage time.

8: BIG CHANCE! Terrible first touch by Danso allows Gomez in on goal, but Roefs does well to stand up tall and make a block.

22: POST! Xhaka feeds Le Fee in space down the left and from his pull back, Isidor's effort is deflected on to the outside of the near post with Verbruggen at full stretch.

45+2: POST! Gross curls a free-kick into the heart of the hosts' area and the totally unmarked Struijk plants a header on to the foot of the post with Roefs motionless.

53: GOAL! The visitors lead as De Cuyper, in acres of space in the box after being found by Gross, drills a low shot past Roefs at his near post after the hosts failed to deal with a long throw.

57: RED CARD! On review, referee Bramall decides Struijk has pulled Isidor to the ground as the striker broke clear on goal and issues a straight red.

90+3: GOAL! Hadjam finds the net after a brilliant counter involving Rutter, who initially does well to hold the ball up, before feeding his fellow sub in space in the box, and from a tight angle the Algerian finds the bottom right-hand corner.

'Sending-off very harsh - on-field decision correct'

Former Premier League referee Mike Dean on Soccer Saturday:

"I do not think it is a sending off. It is very harsh.

"There is a slight barge, I understand that. The referee [Thomas Bramall] has looked at it and thought, 'no, not enough for me'.

"The ball has then gone through to the goalkeeper, he is never going to get the ball, the Sunderland striker [Wilson Isidor], and for me the on-field decision is correct.

"It is not clear and obviously wrong, so why should the VAR [Neil Davies] get involved in my opinion?"

"We felt we were not efficient at that moment.

"It's a learning process. We went with Malick (Fofana), 21, Dayann [Methalie], 20 and Jocelin [Ta Bi], 21, so it's not an easy task to start [your career] in the Premier League in that situation, but this is the challenge.

"We are in our process, the league is tough, the league is relentless, fine details change the momentum and today it wasn't for us."

"No. I never did it [look at the table] and I will never do it because results create judgment. Positive or negative results always create judgment.

"Performances increase improvements. I think that's the main focus for us, we still want to improve, we still want to keep going and we always need to understand it's about doing the basic things right.

"It's about starting from point zero, I mentioned before the game there's no momentum because every team has something special in this league. Every team has a different approach.

"From point zero we have to start again and do the same things again. I think that's crucial and trying to focus on performances, focus on the process and not too much let us (be) affected by the results."

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris will be praying Brian Brobbey's hamstring injury is not too serious after his side drew a blank against the 10 men of Brighton.

The striker, who scored a brilliant hat-trick in the Black Cats' previous outing at Manchester City, picked up the knock while recently on international duty with the Netherlands, meaning a first Premier League start of the season for Wilson Isidor.

The Haiti international nearly gave the hosts an early lead when his sliding opportunity was deflected, while after the break he was involved in Pascal Struijk's dismissal, having been brought down by the Brighton defender while through on goal.

However, Isidor was unable to find the net, meaning Sunderland have now lost back-to-back league games on Wearside without scoring for the first time since April/May 2017 as they slip to 16th in the table.

What the result means and next fixtures...
