articles.title: Chelsea 5-1 Bournemouth: Jordan Henderson's stunning strikes help fast-starting Blues to bounce-back win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Jordan Henderson scores two stunners, Joao Pedro hits a double and Morgan Rogers is on target in thrilling win at Stamford Bridge; Winless Bournemouth undone twice inside first three minutes pulled one back through Evanilson but ultimately blown away
articles.body:
Stunning strikes form Jordan Henderson bookmarked the scoring at Stamford Bridge as Xabi Alonso's side bounced back from their bad loss at Brentford before the international break in style.

After a mixed start to his reign, the Spaniard is now entering a potentially defining run of games which will shape Chelsea's season. This result and performance will fuel belief in the project.

Chelsea were in serious need of a response and got it with a dream start - and more early goals. There were just 65 seconds on the clock when 36-year-old Henderson whipped his first of the afternoon in off a post after good play by Cole Palmer, who had extended his Chelsea contract earlier in the day .

Henderson then turned provider when Morgan Rogers' shot flicked off Antonio Silva and into the far corner. There had been just two minutes and 29 seconds played. It is the earliest Chelsea have ever been 2-0 up in a Premier League game.

Sleepy Bournemouth - who saw Rayan denied by a brilliant one-on-one stop from Emi Martinez just before the break - failed to learn their lesson and incredibly conceded a third just 30 seconds into the second half. Silva's error allowed Pedro Neto to cut the ball back for fit-again Joao Pedro to slam in.

A set-piece scramble saw Evanilson block Moises Caicedo's clearance into the Chelsea net to deny the leaky Blues a clean sheet and there was suddenly nervousness around the ground. But two more quickfire goals ended the contest.

Pep Chavarria's cross for Joao Pedro to tap in his second of the afternoon was excellent. But Henderson's free-kick goal was exquisite. With everyone expecting Palmer to take it on, the veteran midfielder instead produced another spectacular moment.

Alonso's Chelsea may not be perfect. But they sure are exciting to watch.

2: GOAL! It's a perfect start for Chelsea and Henderson. Palmer makes progress into the box then cuts it back to the midfielder who whips a stunning shot in off the far post!

3: GOAL! Chelsea are in dreamland as a Rogers shot flicks off Silva and into the far corner. There's a VAR check for offside on Joao Pedro, who was jostling with Silva but the goal stands!

6: WIDE! Rayan is played into the box by Marcus Tavernier but he lashes wastefully wide of the near post.

23: CLOSE! Henderson lobs a shot towards the far corner from the edge of the box but a deflection takes it narrowly wide.

36: DOUBLE SAVE! Adrien Truffert curls a pass through for Rayan to run onto but Martinez dashes out and sticks out a left arm to block the one-on-one shot. Ryan Christie is onto the rebound 25 yards out but Martinez gets up quickly to stop the next one.

46: GOAL! Another lightning start from Chelsea! Just 30 seconds into the second half, Silva's mistake allows Neto to cut the ball back for Joao Pedro to slam in Chelsea's third!

51: GOAL! Bournemouth pull one back when Evanilson blocks Caicedo's clearance into the net after a flicked-on corner causes chaos in the Chelsea six-yard box.

67: GOAL! Bournemouth were piling on the pressure but Rogers feeds Chavarria who punches a first-time pass across the face of goal for Joao Pedro to tuck in!

70: GOAL! Henderson bends a brilliant free-kick in from 25 yards after Palmer is hauled down. A sensational strike!

Alonso pleased with 'very complete' performance

"Today it was a very complete performance. We were in control for most parts of the game, so I am happy with that. We have had a good stability in defence as well, just a couple of situations in the first half and the second one, after conceding for 3-1. For minutes until the 4-1 we were not in control, but overall, happy with the game. It's many positives to take for the future, and other ones to keep it going."

On Henderson's performance: "We signed him for everything and if he's able to score two beauties, as today, we are more than happy for him, but apart from the goals, he's done many, many good things.

"Taking away the goals, it was a very midfielder performance, always being involved in the action, always giving solutions to the team-mates. The way he plays, he needs to communicate with the players around, with Moi [Moises Caicedo].

"It was important for Moi to pay 65 minutes. We were in a situation that we could adjust his load, so many, many good news today, and we keep going."

Analysis: Chelsea show they're ready to attack key run of games

Sky Sports' Peter Smith at Stamford Bridge:

Chelsea's season is set to be shaped by the run of games they have before the November international break. After a mixed start to Xabi Alonso's reign, he is in need of a strong run in the Premier League to boost the bid to return to Champions League football, while a Carabao Cup tie at Liverpool could be a launchpad for early silverware.

His Chelsea side showed how they're going to go about it on Saturday, blowing away Bournemouth with their attacking power.

Joao Pedro is fit again and still firing. Cole Palmer was classy and looks recovered from the issue which forced him out of England duty and buoyed by a new Chelsea contract. Morgan Rogers is in form and connecting with both in style. And a certain Jordan Henderson has developed an ability to crack in stunning goals.

Moises Caicedo's first start brought extra punch in midfield. There was, though, some nervousness when Bournemouth bundled one back, such has been Chelsea's poor defensive record this season. But while Alonso was preparing a double change to intervene, Chelsea scored two more. That looks like it will be their way for now, as they aim to blast their way into a position to push for success this season.

Rose: We were not sharp enough - but I'm still confident

" We played not good. We knew Chelsea is a team that starts well and score many goals at beginnings of games. It is our responsibility we didn't react the right way on this information.

"The last games we mostly had good performances and struggled in some situations and got punished. Today we struggled for long periods in the game.

"We were not ready, we were not sharp enough. Even our pressing was not Bournemouth-like in many situations. It can happen. We need to face the reality - three points after six games. But we're going to stick together. We knew it was going to be a demanding season and we have many games where we can show up, do it better and get on a run."

On being under pressure: "I know this business. We played five games well. Drew three times, lost two times. Now the first time we played not the way we want to see us. It's not up to me when rumours start about the coach. I can deal with this. I know the team, the way we work, I'm confident, I believe in the club and the team that we're going to do it.

"We can see the table, we know how it works in the Premier League. Now it's up to us to prove and show we can handle the situation."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Aston Villa 2-2 Brentford: Unbeaten Bees find leveller through Kristoffer Ajer to halt Villa turnaround at Villa Park
articles.summary: Match report and free highlights as Aston Villa and Brentford shared four goals in a  2-2 draw at Villa Park; Yehor Yarmoliuk put the Bees in front early but Nicolas Jackson levelled; Kristoffer Ajer cancelled out John McGinn’s strike; Visitors stay fourth
articles.body:
Brentford's fine start to the season was reflected in their confidence. They pressed Villa high from the outset and it brought the opening goal after Tyrone Mings lost possession in a dangerous area. Yehor Yarmoliuk smashed the loose ball into Zion Suzuki's net.

But Villa levelled within 88 seconds when Emi Buendia's shot was deflected into the path of Nicolas Jackson who did the rest from close range. Buendia, Johan Manzambi on his first home start, and John McGinn all then had chances for Villa before the break.

McGinn's deflected strike did give Villa the lead in the 77th minute but once again the response was swift, this time Keith Andrews' side finding the equaliser. Ajer unexpectedly burst through from deep down the left channel and forced the ball home to stun Villa Park.

The point means Brentford remain undefeated six games into the Premier League season and maintain their place among the top four. Meanwhile, Villa's stuttering start to the campaign continues under Unai Emery with just one win from their first six.

10 - GOAL! Yarmoliuk fired Brentford in front early in the game

12 - GOAL! Jackson latched onto Buendia's deflected effort

31 - MISS! Buendia skied his shot after Manzambi was denied

45+5 - SAVES! Jackson and McGinn both denied by Kelleher

73 - OVER! Anthony headed over Jensen's cross at the far post

77 - GOAL! McGinn's strike deflected in for Villa to take the lead

79 - GOAL! Ajer burst through from deep to level it up once more

Brentford head coach Keith Andrews speaking in the press conference:

"We could've won it, could've lost it and I'm a tad disappointed that we couldn't take advantage of situations in the last 10 to 15 minutes where I felt we were coming on strong and had the opportunity to win the game.

"But to come away to a club that is playing in the Champions League, won the Europa League, with a manager who has just been nominated for the Ballon d'Or [for coach of the year] it probably says where we're at, at the moment."

It was Ajer who McGinn's shot deflected off for what briefly looked to be the winning goal for Villa but the Norwegian defender swiftly made amends at the other end with the equalising goal. Speaking to Andrews afterwards, he was fulsome in his praise.

"He's a very professional leader in our dressing room and club, you know, for numerous years now. His game has gone to a different level over the course of the last year.

"I just think he's in those peak years of his career. He is trusted by me, by the staff, by his teammates. He has gone to a World Cup and had a brilliant World Cup. I think that can only give you real confidence in what you're doing and how you do it."

Analysis by Sky Sports' Adam Bate at Villa Park:

"At Villa Park, we have played three matches and we did not win until now," said Unai Emery after seeing his side held by Kristoffer Ajer's goal that earned Brentford their 2-2 draw. This place was once a fortress but it is proving trickier for a much-changed squad.

There will be patience with the players, particularly given that Nicolas Jackson, scorer of Aston Villa's opening goal, has made a promising start and there is such excitement about the potential of talented new signings like Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye.

But could the empty North Stand be another factor in their home form too? Villa Park feels unusually open with no supporters there and the Brentford supporters were likening the atmosphere to that of a library right from the early stages of the contest.

"It just feels wrong, doesn't it? I don't know what it is," said Bees boss Keith Andrews. "I have got a little bit of OCD, so maybe it's that, if there's a whole stand missing, it doesn't quite sit well with me. Naturally, it's not going to generate the type of atmosphere.

"I have to say, I love coming here. When I was growing up as a kid, some Irish legends played here, Ray Houghton, Paul McGrath, Andy Townsend, so it's always been a special place for me and you can feel the history of it. With a stand missing, it is a bit different."

Emery has been sanguine about the situation publicly, accepting that it is one step back to take two forwards by increasing the capacity. But Villa Park is less claustrophobic for its visitors right now and that is far from ideal for a club so reliant on its home form.

articles.standfirst: El entrenador babazorro elogió la actuación del Atlético y no cree que haya motivos para la preocupación tras cuatro jornadas sin ganar
articles.summary: El entrenador babazorro elogió la actuación del Atlético y no cree que haya motivos para la preocupación tras cuatro jornadas sin ganar
articles.body: Quique Sánchez Flores compareció al término del partido para valorar la derrota del Alavés ante el Atlético. El técnico madrileño echó en falta una mayor precisión de su equipo con balón, al mismo tiempo que lamentó el gol en la recta final del encuentro. Análisis: “Hemos competido bien ante un rival que nos ha exigido mucho y ha hecho un gran partido. Han tocado el balón rápido y con mucho criterio. Ha sido una lástima encajar cerca del final. La expulsión ha venido cuando teníamos varios cambios preparados y me hubiera gustado ver ese partido con once jugadores. Era el momento de ponernos a su altura física. Con un jugador menos, nos hemos visto en una situación límite y nos hemos alejado de nuestras posibilidades”. Posesión del Atlético: “Entiendo que han jugado bastante bien y no ha sido nuestro mejor partido con la pelota. Se han dado las dos cosas. Nos han hecho correr y hemos perdido rápido el balón”. Expulsión: “No la he visto. Es una de esas jugadas que el jugador no quiere hacer. Me han dicho que hay una acción de Lookman en el primer tiempo parecida donde el criterio del VAR es diferente. Si es así, nos duele”. Cuatro jornadas sin ganar: “No hay preocupación. Queremos que el equipo sea consciente y humilde respecto a sus posibilidades. Estamos en esta racha incómoda que no nos tiene que alejar de nuestro objetivo. Hemos perdido contra un equipo Champions”.

articles.title: El Barça no tiene espera: le van los goles tempraneros
articles.standfirst: En ocho de los 9 encuentros que ha disputado ha marcado antes del minuto 25
articles.summary: En ocho de los 9 encuentros que ha disputado ha marcado antes del minuto 25
articles.body: El Barça no tiene espera. No aguarda a que la afición haya acabado de sentarse cuando ya ha marcado... Esta tarde, contra el Getafe, Anthony Gordon superó a Soria cuando apenas habían transcurrido dos minutos del encuentro de LaLiga. Pero los goles tempraneros son ya una tónica esta temporada. Tardar en entrar en los partidos era una de las quejas y lamentos de Flick hacia sus futbolistas del curso pasado, y claramente han corregido su forma de saltar al césped. El Barcelona, líder, ha celebrado un tanto antes del minuto 25 en 8 de los 9 encuentros que ha disputado esta temporada: ocho de LaLiga y uno de la Champions League. Únicamente en el compromiso contra el Athletic se demoró un poco: Raphinha inauguró el marcador en la primera mitad, pero lo hizo en el 37'. En el resto de encuentros, el combinado culé vio puerta muy pronto, aunque en dos compromisos sufrió que el rival le superara antes: en los choques contra el Rayo y el Sevilla. Pero logró remontar gracias a su pronta reacción. El gol del internacional inglés contra el Getafe es, no obstante, el más tempranero, ya que apenas habían transcurrido dos minutos del cruce en el Spotify Camp Nou. Raphinha marcó en el 3' contra el Feyenoord en la Champions, Espart vio puerta en el 5' frente al Levante, Lamine Yamal abrió el marcador contra el Valencia en el 6'... Flick había recriminado, el curso pasado, en más de una ocasión a sus hombres que salían al campo desconectados y desconcentrados. Asignatura aprobada. Con excelente nota. La diana de Gordon es, además, la primera que marca el inglés con la camiseta del Barça. Había dado cinco asistencias en LaLiga y no había visto puerta. Esta tarde contra los de Bordalás se quitó la espina que tenía clavada.

articles.title: Preston North End 0-1 Millwall: Camiel Neghli's late strike inflicts opening defeat for new Lilywhites boss Graham Alexander
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Preston North End and Millwall at The Den on Saturday; Camiel Neghli's late strike ensured Graham Alexander's first Lilywhite games ended in defeat
articles.body:
It was coolness personified from the Dutch-born Algerian, who slotted Luke Cundle's cut-back into the far corner from just inside the box for what turned out to be a 79th-minute winner.

Alexander was at Deepdale for 10 years, making 400 appearances for the Lancashire outfit, and he stood on the touchline as their manager for the first time since leaving Bradford, who were at the top of League One when he departed.

On this evidence, the 55-year-old will have his work cut out as he hopes to turn around Preston's fortunes with the Lilywhites currently sitting rock bottom of the Championship.

He came undone against a former Preston manager in Alex Neil, who would have been delighted to have ended his three-match winless run with a hard-fought, but deserved, away victory.

Alexander's new era nearly got off to the worst possible start as Tairyk Arconte slotted past Daniel Iversen inside 30 seconds having latched onto Neghli's defence-splitting pass, only to be denied by the offside flag.

A buoyant atmosphere pre-game was quickly dimmed and Neghli tested Iversen with a well-struck volley from the edge of the box on 10 minutes as Preston defenders struggled to clear their lines.

The home side were all at sea again in the 16th minute as Kyrell Lisbie thundered against the bar from close range at the near post, reacting quickest to Lyndon Dykes' header forward.

Preston's first real chance of note came after 23 minutes as Harry Clarke dragged wide from an acute angle after Jusef Erabi's shot was blocked by defender Jake Cooper.

On the half-hour mark, though, the pitch opened up for Preston again as Andrija Vukcevic found Callum Lang, who fizzed a shot wide from just outside the box.

The best chance for the hosts fell on the stroke of half-time as Caleb Taylor woefully misjudged a bouncing ball, allowing Erabi in on goal, but the Swede struck straight at Filip Marschall.

Millwall started the second period like they did the first, on the front foot, and Iversen had to be alert to keep out Lisbie at the near post as he turned Zak Sturge's cross towards goal.

North End did almost take the lead on the counter, however, as Lang teed up Alfie Devine but the ball was slightly behind the former Tottenham man and he dragged his effort wide.

It looked like the game was fizzling out until Neghli provided a ruthless killer instinct from 16 yards, his third goal of the season, much to the delight of the travelling fans behind the goal.

"At half-time, 0-0 or 1-1 would have been a fair scoreline but the first half was really positive. I thought we were slightly the better team without taking that lead.

"In the second half, we had an opportunity after about 10 or 15 minutes but apart from that I thought it was a transitional game, attritional, lots of challenges and competitiveness. There was a threat from their set-pieces and I don't think ours were good enough or competitive enough but, at that stage, it was 0-0 or 1-0 and we fell on the wrong side of that line.

"We have to try and improve, obviously. We have to improve on both sides of the game. With our defensive structure - which I thought was really good today to be honest, so that's something we have to maintain - there was a slight glitch in our goal, which is something we can fix and remedy straight away because when we see it on Monday, we'll see it straight away."

"In the first half, I thought the game was quite loose for both teams. We scored in the first two minutes and it got disallowed for offside, we hit the underside of the bar, we probably should score, we hit the post, so we certainly carried a threat, but I thought Preston were a little bit threatening in the first half as well.

"We changed it a little bit, put an extra midfielder in the middle, put a striker up through the side, put a bit of pace on the flanks, so it gave us a little bit more control of the pitch but probably meant we carried a little bit less of a threat. I thought when the subs came on as well, I thought that they helped us."

articles.title: Sheffield United 3-0 Lincoln City: Patrick Bamford scores twice as Blades bounce back from two straight defeats
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Sheffield United and Lincoln City at Bramall Lane on Saturday; Patrick Bamford scores twice and Tahith Chong also on target as Blades win first league game in three
articles.body:
The result, who also saw Tahith Chong on the scoresheet, ended a three-match losing run for Chris Wilder's men in all competitions against a side which had won three of their previous four away matches.

Lincoln applied early pressure and had a great chance to open the scoring when Rob Street headed the ball back to Sonny Bradley, who headed over from the edge of the six-yard box. It was a chance that the skipper will surely feel he should have at least put on target.

Before then, United goalkeeper Michael Cooper comfortably dealt with a low shot from Conor McGrandles and an Adam Reach free-kick.

The home side then grew into the game with Joe Rothwell putting a long-range drive only a fraction wide and Ben Brereton Diaz firing straight at George Wickens in the Lincoln goal before they drew first blood.

The goal came two minutes before the break when Rothwell found Sam McCallum on the left-hand side of the area and he squared to Bamford, who found the net with a deft near-post flick.

Rothwell fired over from a good position soon after the restart before the Blades increased their lead.

Chong struck in the 52nd minute when firing under Wickens from a tight angle after receiving the ball from Rothwell.

Lincoln made a triple substitution shortly after the hour-mark with Mikel Ladefoged, Yunus Konak and Chiedozie Ogbene all joining the action.

The changes did little to help Lincoln's cause, however, with the hosts continuing to hold the upper hand and it was no surprise when they went further ahead.

The third goal came in the 77th minute when Brereton Diaz swung the ball over from the right wing and Bamford beat Wickens with a well-executed far-post volley.

Ogbene threatened on a couple of occasions down the left wing, without seriously putting the defence under threat.

The Imps had failed to build on their promising start and United showed little sign of allowing them to find a way back into the game.

When the visitors did have a chance in the closing stages, Ladefoged spurned a golden opportunity to pull a goal back.

Cooper did superbly well to keep out the striker's close-range effort and when the rebound fell to Ladefoged, he somehow screwed his shot wide.

United leapfrogged their opponents into 13th place, while Lincoln slipped down to 15th after a second successive defeat.

"We needed a clean sheet, we needed a big performance. The team that we were playing - one of the best away records in the division - hasn't just been given them and wasn't given their 100-plus points last season.

"Well coached last year, well coached this year, awkward opposition, honest, played to a way that's really, really effective.

"Regardless of the name of the football club or where they've been, or how many years they've not been in the Championship or if they've never been in the Championship, they're here on merit and they're going to pose a lot of teams problems this season.

"And we understood that challenge right away through the two or three weeks that we had to prepare for it.

"The pressure obviously has cranked up over the last two or three weeks. We're after that winning feeling and we've got it today.

"We needed to play well. Players needed to up their game because we've got a lot of good players.

"It's always easy to play when the champagne's dripping from the ceiling. This was a tough game and we had to show what we were about individually, our mentality and most importantly our personality.

"It was a bit scruffy at the start, which I think you could understand that off the back of the last two losses, but once we got the first goal, I thought we were we had control of the game.

"It's a dangerous opposition. And we needed big performances from everybody, the coaches, the manager and the players."

"I thought for half an hour, I thought we were a fair game for being level. We wanted to come and try and create some nervousness.

"We understood there's a bit of tension around the position that Sheffield United are in and where they want to be. I thought we did that.

"We changed our structure a little bit. I thought we had a couple of phases of play, but then a sucker punch.

"We know the quality of the league. We understand that if we give good players time and space, they're going to be able to hurt us.

"But most definitely, we'll watch them goals back and we'll find ways that we could have been better to stop.

"We're going to have some tough games, some tough days. We understand that we don't want them and we're never going to settle for them.

"But we know there's a group of players there that are capable of coming to Sheffield United and getting a result."

articles.title: Middlesbrough 1-0 Wolverhampton Wanderers: Will Lankshear scores again as Boro celebrate 150th anniversary game with a win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Middlesbrough and Wolverhampton Wanderers at the Riverside Stadium on Saturday; Will Lankshear scored his ninth goal of the season to seal a narrow win for Boro
articles.body:
This is Boro's 150th season since the club was founded to enable the cricketers from Middlesbrough Cricket Club to play an alternative sport in the winter months, and the game with Wolves was selected as the official anniversary fixture.

A sold-out crowd helped mark the occasion, six days after a host of former players returned to the Riverside for a Legacy Game, and Lankshear's header from Tommy Conway's cross ensured the home fans went home happy.

The win enabled Middlesbrough to climb above West Ham into second position in the Sky Bet Championship table, just two points behind leaders Swansea.

Wolves were second best for most of the afternoon as they suffered a second league defeat since their relegation last season.

Prior to the game, Boro's fans in the South Stand unfurled a huge mural paying tribute to the club's founding players, and the current generation seemed to be inspired by the celebratory mood as they made a bright start.

Lankshear curled an early free-kick over the top before forcing Jose Sa into a smart save down to his left as he fired in an angled strike from the left of the penalty area.

Marshall Munetsi headed Rodrigo Gomes' cross well wide as Wolves made a rare foray into the Boro box, but with the home side asking most of the questions, Sebastian Berhalter dragged a long-range shot wide.

Berhalter was involved again shortly afterwards, swinging in a cross that Adilson Malanda headed straight at Sa, but the first half ended with Boro goalkeeper Radek Vitek making his first save of the afternoon as he parried away Munetsi's 25-yard strike.

The Teessiders reasserted themselves at the start of the second period, though, and claimed a deserved lead three minutes before the hour mark.

Conway did superbly to create sufficient space on the left-hand side to stand up a cross to the back post, and having peeled behind Hugo Bueno, Lankshear outjumped the Wolves full-back to powerfully head home his seventh league goal of the season.

Boro almost doubled their lead 10 minutes later, but while Aidan Morris slipped a perfect slide-rule pass into the path of Berhalter, his fellow American could only direct his shot straight at Sa.

The home side came close again with two minutes left, but while substitute Kyle Joseph thumped a header against the underside of the crossbar, the ball stayed out.

"It feels like a good win against a very good side, one of the favourites to win the division. Over 90 minutes, I thought it was a fair result.

"I think we were the better team, and I thought before the goal we were absolutely brilliant in everything, except maybe we could have got some more chances from the quality we had.

"Transitions, playing through them, playing high, winning balls, it was absolutely brilliant. I can't really remember a chance they had.

"Then, after the goal, we showed as good as you can ever do when you are 1-0 up - defending while still having some transitions. You always want to kill the game off, but that is never easy. We defended really well."

"We knew it was going to be difficult. Middlesbrough have a good team. In the first half Middlesbrough had more of the ball and we were focused on our defensive organisation.

"They didn't create a lot of clear chances to score.

"At half-time, I talked with the players and told them to manage things better and take time with the ball. We had a strong reaction after Middlesbrough scored. Only a big team with a lot of soul and a lot of quality would react in the way we reacted.

"We didn't take the best decision with our final pass or cross, and we didn't quite get enough players into the box to fight to be able to score. But we could still have scored one goal and drawn the game.

"It is a defeat - I'm not happy with the result, but I am happy with the reaction of the team after they went behind. We reacted and competed to the end, and if we do that, we are going to win more games than we lose, that's for sure."

articles.title: Watford 0-4 Burnley: Reo Hatate on target as Clarets collect first Championship win at ninth time of asking
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Watford and Burnley at Vicarage Road on Saturday; goals from Jacob Bruun Larsen, Zeki Amdouni, Reo Hatate and Marcus Edwards helped the Clarets emphatically end their winless start
articles.body:
While Alessio Dionisi's fifth defeat in six games cranked up the pressure on the Hornets head coach, counterpart Nicky Hayen's first three-point haul lifted Burnley off the Championship seabed.

Three goals in the space of 12 first-half minutes put the visitors out of sight and extended the Hornets' wretched defensive record to 29 weeks without a clean sheet.

When Stoke won 2-1 at Vicarage Road last month, it ended 251 days without a win on the road for the Potters. Here, Watford extended more charity to the Clarets, who ended 241 days without an away win comfortably.

On the day Watford paid tribute to former goalkeeper and two-time player of the season Kevin Miller, who died suddenly aged 57 last month, Dionisi needed a lift after an injury-ravaged start to the season.

But his mood soon darkened after just 13 minutes as Burnley scored from their first meaningful excursion into the box, Reo Hatate feeding Jacob Bruun Larsen to sweep home his first goal in 39 appearances for the club.

Six minutes later, Larsen was close to adding a second, as Watford keeper Federico Ravaglia brilliantly parried his fierce effort, but Zeki Amdouni was first to react and bundled home his third goal of the season to double Burnley's advantage.

Worse was to follow for the home side as Hatate was afforded generous space to pick his spot from 15 yards and make it 3-0 after 25 minutes.

The defensive meltdown was too much for the irate Watford supporters, with loud refrains of 'Sack the board' and chants against owner Gino Pozzo amid the pockets of booing.

When these sides last met 18 months ago, the Hornets finished with nine men after Moussa Sissoko and Edo Kayembe were sent off in a fractious contest, but this one was effectively decided inside the opening half-hour.

Dionisi's decision to withdraw Spanish playmaker Iker Bravo was howled down by his own supporters, and although Watford went through the motions of a fightback after the break, they never threatened to reverse the damage.

Mamadou Doumbia's header was parried by Gregoire Coudert and the Mali International should have done better from another opportunity.

At the other end, Ravaglia did well to keep out Clarets substitute Marcus Edwards' free-kick, but three minutes from the end the unmarked Edwards rifled home a superb volley to complete Watford's miserable afternoon.

On Watford's latest official club podcast, executive chairman Scott Duxbury warned: "This year, no excuses, we've got to achieve our potential and have a successful season. I'm not setting any parameters at this stage but we've got players here who demand it."

"In football it's normal. It's probably better to say only one thing - I'm sorry for this match.

"I'm very angry because after 30 minutes the match was finished, it was impossible (to come back).

"It's difficult to explain - I know my players and one month ago it was different. It's impossible to win if the team is not stronger.

"Five matches out of six with no points is not good, but I believe in my team and I believe in my job. I'm here and we work every to improve: now it is important to work well, to work better."

"There were a lot of reasons why we went eight games without a win.

"I came in when pre-season had already started and I worked with eight or nine players who left during the transfer window. Then a lot of players came in who weren't fit.

"We couldn't win a game but I never doubted us and I will never doubt us because I know what we're capable of.

"I'm not going to lie - it wasn't the start that I expected, but I never panicked. When we lose three times, I'm not the guy who's going to sit in the corner because every day I come back with a new energy.

"Let's hope this is the start of something beautiful, but it's just one win. I'm always convinced that my style is the right style for this team and this club.

"We have to be humble but the players can enjoy this victory because it's eight months since the last one and that's a long time."

articles.title: Bolton Wanderers 1-2 Stoke City: Lamine Cisse, Ben Wilmot secure victory for Mark Robins' 10-man Potters
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bolton Wanderers and Stoke City at the Toughsheet Community Stadium on Saturday; Lamine Cisse and Ben Wilmot score as Mark Robins' Potters seal a first away win over the Trotters since 1990
articles.body:
Mark Robins' in-form side played for 70 minutes without Maksym Talovierov after the defender's dismissal for bringing down Kyliane Dong.

However, the Potters shrugged off the disadvantage to gain a first win in Bolton since October 1990, when 1966 World Cup hero Alan Ball was in charge.

Cisse fired the visitors in front in first-half stoppage time before Wilmot piled on the agony for Wanderers boss Steven Schumacher after 64 minutes.

The Potters' fifth win in six games lifted them up to fourth while Bolton drop to 17th.

The Trotters kicked off bidding for three successive Championship wins for the first time in 12 years, and they should have been in front after nine minutes.

Ethan Erhahon's defensive splitting pass sent Dong racing clear but the Augsburg loanee's shot was saved by Viktor Johansson's left leg.

Stoke responded four minutes later when Wilmot fired into the side netting, but their bid to break a 10-game Bolton hoodoo appeared to plunge when Talovierov was red-carded by referee Thomas Kirk.

The Ukrainian defender was adjudged to have denied Dong a goalscoring opportunity with a last-ditch tackle fractionally outside the penalty area.

Wales international Josh Sheehan fired the resulting free-kick narrowly wide and Wanderers went close again through Gaizka Larrazabal, but wasted a further chance to take the lead after 31 minutes.

Ruben Rodrigues' right-wing cross was a beauty but striker Sam Dalby headed it down and over the bar from five yards.

Stoke then took the lead against the run of play. Ethan Galbraith supplied the assist and Cisse stayed onside to curl a low right-foot shot beyond Gavin Bazunu for his first goal of the campaign.

They should have added a second goal eight minutes after the re-start. Again, Cisse was the dangerman, cutting inside and driving an effort against Bazunu's left upright.

Bazuna, playing for the first time since boycotting the Republic of Ireland's Nations League games with Israel, then saved substitute Luca Bambino's follow-up.

However, the Potters' deservedly doubled their advantage when Jack McGlynn whipped in a free-kick from the Bolton left and Wilmot headed home powerfully in front of 4,600 City supporters.

It could have been three two minutes later but Cisse's latest attempt was saved by Bazunu.

Canadian substitute Thelonius Bair gave Bolton hope of a very late comeback when he scored his first goal for Wanderers in the second minute of stoppage time.

Dalby then headed straight at Johansson but Stoke held on for a deserved win.

"We made key errors at bad times. It was a big opportunity for us, especially when they went down to 10 men.

"It should have been the catalyst to go on and win the game. We knew it wouldn't be easy just because they had a man sent off.

"They were going to make it hard for us but when we got the big chances we had to score.

"We had to capitalise but we didn't. And giving the goal away before half-time changed everything. Their team talk is a lot easier. The second goal was just a poor decision from us.

"They showed more experience and more quality and more energy. And that's the most disappointing thing because we knew this was a big opportunity for us."

"For me, there is a lot of improvement there. We are showing a lot of bravery, a lot of quality and they are showing they can score goals. But they are also showing they can keep them out.

"We have some good positive points at the moment, but it is a tough league and you don't take anything for granted.

"It was disappointing the way it [the red card] came about. I thought we had covering defenders that were coming round.

"It spoiled the game from our perspective. Bolton have some good players and wanted a basketball game and wanted it open.

"I wanted us to come up against them and try to beat them and do things in this game we haven't necessarily done. But football doesn't give you everything you want.

"So, we had to grind out a result and grind out a performance."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Derby County 1-1 Wrexham: Ollie Rathbone strikes late to earn a point for the Red Dragons at Pride Park
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Derby County and Wrexham at Pride Park on Saturday; Sam Szmodics put the Rams in front, but Ollie Rathbone scored an 88th-minute equaliser for the visitors
articles.body:
The Rams were on course for victory through Sam Szmodics' superb early strike only for the Welsh side to rescue a point two minutes from the end.

Both teams created chances in an open game, but the finishing lacked the quality Szmodics showed when he beat Anthony Patterson with an unstoppable shot.

It looked like it was going to be a frustrating afternoon for Wrexham until Kieffer Moore set up Rathbone for a close-range finish to leave Derby still waiting for that elusive home victory.

Derby had started positively and deservedly went ahead in the ninth minute following a clinical counter-attack.

Mo Fuseini sprinted from deep inside his own half to release Szmodics, who cut inside before unleashing a rising drive past Patterson.

The Dragons responded through Jacques Ekomie, who ran into the Derby box and fired in a low shot which Josh Vickers did well to palm away.

Vickers rescued Derby again when Callum O'Hare's shot took a deflection, forcing the goalkeeper into a reflex save and Issa Kabore put the rebound into the side-netting.

Szmodics was close to a second in the 35th minute when he pounced on a loose ball and curled a shot just wide of Patterson's left post.

The first half ended with the visitors catching the Rams on the break, but O'Hare's shot was deflected over for a corner which came to nothing.

Fuseini's pace had caused problems from the start and the winger made another run at the Wrexham defence in the 58th minute, but his shot was straight at Patterson.

The away side had got into good positions without making them count and Danny Imray wasted another chance with an overhit cross before Carlton Morris fired over at the other end.

Wrexham had a good effort to level in the 75th minute when O'Hare found space, but blazed over from 12 yards.

Derby almost made them pay with Bobby Clark getting in on the Wrexham right and hitting a low shot which was deflected narrowly wide.

After the home survived a scramble inside the six-yard box, Ekomie lashed a shot over and they were heading for defeat until Rathbone came to the rescue in the 88th minute.

The Rams had defended strongly throughout but when Imray crossed from the right, Moore rose to head the ball down and Rathbone nipped in to beat Vickers.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portuguese Football Federation provisionally suspends forward after walkout following disagreement with manager Jorge Jesus
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo walked out on the Portugal national team after accusing Jorge Jesus of reneging on an agreement to bring him as a substitute in a win over Norway; 41-year-old went on to release near 2,000-word statement in which he accused the manager of a "breach of trust"
articles.body:
Ronaldo left the Portugal squad after he was an unused substitute for a 2-1 win away to Norway in the Nations League on September 27.

The 41-year-old, who has scored a record-breaking 146 goals in 234 appearances for his country, subsequently issued a near 2,000-word statement saying he withdrew from the squad after a "breach of trust" between him and head coach Jorge Jesus.

The Portuguese Football Federation has now acted, saying in a statement reported by Lisbon-based newspaper A Bola : "Disciplinary proceedings were initiated against Cristiano Ronaldo, by decision of the non-professional section, on October 9, with the objective of ascertaining the potential disciplinary relevance of the facts reported on October 7.

"Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of initiation, a non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined and the proceedings were given urgent status.

"The proceedings were sent, on October 10, to the disciplinary instruction committee of the FPF (Portuguese Football Federation), with publicity excluded until the end of the investigation."

Ronaldo missed Portugal's following two fixtures, wins over Denmark and Norway, which left them top of Group A4 with four straight wins, fuelling speculation his international career could be over.

Jesus left the door open to the veteran forward in a press conference after Sunday's win against Norway, saying: "If he wants to, he'll return to the national team."

Along with his criticism of Jesus, Ronaldo did apologise for his actions - and asked the Portugal FA to punish him and spare him any leniency.

Ronaldo returned to Al Nassr and scored for his Saudi Arabian club on Friday in his first appearance since his walkout.

Ronaldo claims coach had 'broken his word to me'

Jesus previously denied there was a rift between him and Ronaldo but his future is far from clear following his decision to air his grievances in public.

In his statement to his 679 million Instagram followers, Ronaldo said: "If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team."

Ronaldo also claimed in his statement that Jesus had told him he would play 30 minutes against Norway on the day of the game, only to go back on his word.

He added: "Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from half-time onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn't called on," Ronaldo said. "The coach had broken his word to me."

According to the latest opinion polls in Portugal, most football fans are supporting Jesus in his dispute with Ronaldo.

The eight points Jesus 'agreed' to say to the media

Ronaldo and Jesus, who used to work together at Al Nassr, subsequently held a meeting, which was also attended by the sporting director of the Saudi Pro League club, Simao Coutinho.

According to Ronaldo's statement, Jesus agreed to clarify the situation and say that his captain never demanded minutes and that it was a mistake to let him warm up without bringing him on.

Ronaldo says an eight-point document was drawn up to summarise what had been discussed in a subsequent meeting between Jesus, Al Nassr sporting director Coutinho and Tiago Craveiro, the player's strategic adviser.

However, Ronaldo felt the Portugal head coach's press conference bore no reflection to the conversation they had shared, which he claims ended in Jesus asking him for a hug.

"I heard expressions and an aggressiveness that I do not believe I deserved, an attitude of 'I want, I can and I command' that he never showed me, not even remotely, in private the day before," said Ronaldo.

He added: "It was the second time he had broken his word to me. I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises."

Jesus denied that any such agreement had been made with the player in a later press conference.

How Ronaldo nearly retired from international football

Ronaldo publicly admitted earlier in this international break that he considered retiring from international football following the World Cup.

His statement on Instagram reveals that he had written his retirement statement only to be talked out of it by the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, Pedro Proenca, on the plane back from North America.

Ronaldo says Proenca then asked him for his opinion on Jesus becoming Portugal's next manager.

"I told [him] that, in my opinion, it would be the right choice," Ronaldo said. "That is why, on the day the current head coach was presented, I was genuinely happy with the choice. It was the right option, as the results are confirming."

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portuguese FA provisionally suspend forward after leaving international camp
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving his country's international camp last month.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving his country's international camp last month.

The 41-year-old captain walked out of Portugal's Nations League squad in September after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark.

In a lengthy statement, the Al-Nassr forward later explained he left because Portugal coach Jorge Jesus twice "broke his word", accusing him of an "absolute breach of trust".

In a statement, the FPF said a "provisional suspension" was issued on 9 October and they had marked the case as "urgent".

The FPF's rules state any player who fails to appear or walks out on international duties faces a ban of one to six months, as well as a fine.

Pedro Proenc, president of the FPF, told Portuguese outlet Record: , external "This is a time for calm and composure. We are all sitting down together at the table.

"There is a strong desire to have our captain back with us. There will be a normal disciplinary process."

Ronaldo accepted accountability and apologised to his team-mates and fans for his actions, before adding he deserved to be punished.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner also confirmed he would not be retiring from international football as he continues to chase down 1000 career goals.

Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances - both men's world records - helping them win Euro 2016 and the Nations League twice.

He considered retiring from international football after the World Cup in the summer but opted to continue.

Ronaldo returned to action last week, scoring his 980th career goal in a 3-0 win for Al-Nassr over Diriyah Club.

Two icons, a glorious farewell and a potentially bitter ending

The Ronaldo saga has been rumbling on for some time, with many fans critical of former Portugal boss Roberto Martinez's insistence on starting Ronaldo at this summer's World Cup.

Things came to a head on 4 October when Ronaldo was an unused substitute in the Nations League win over Norway. The player subsequently left camp after finding out he would also not start against Denmark in November.

Ronaldo then published a near 2,000-word statement on Instagram slamming Jesus.

He apologised to fans and team-mates while dismissing any suggestion that he had played his last match for Portugal.

"We will have one or more farewell matches, there will be time for that," the statement said.

Manager Jesus had said the door remains open for Ronaldo to return if he chooses to, but has not commented on his latest statement.

Portuguese football journalist Jose Manuel Delgado told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I don't think there is a way back. In the statement, Ronaldo says he will return to the national team but at the same time he calls Jesus a liar three times.

"In the polls in Portugal, only 15% of the Portuguese were on Ronaldo's side and people think we owe him a lot but his time is already done and he must understand it.

"The problem is that Ronaldo does not understand it, he wants to keep playing as if he was 24, not 41.

"Things will never be the same again. No matter what happens, no matter if he plays again or if you have a game to say goodbye to Ronaldo things will never be the same.

"What Ronaldo did for Portuguese football is unique and incredible and we must thank him for all the service he gave to Portugal. But at 41, he has no place in the best XI of Portugal."

articles.title: Portugal suspends Ronaldo and initiates disciplinary proceedings after walkout
articles.summary: The Portuguese Football Federation has suspended Cristiano Ronaldo for walking out on the team and initiated disciplinary proceedings.
articles.body: LISBON, Portugal — The Portuguese Football Federation has suspended Cristiano Ronaldo for walking out on the team and initiated disciplinary proceedings. The case has been referred to its disciplinary investigation committee and its findings will remain confidential until its conclusions are reached, the federation said in a statement Saturday. The 41-year-old Ronaldo left the Portugal camp during the international window in a dispute with new coach Jorge Jesus over his lack of playing time in the Nations League. In the three games Ronaldo was either an unused substitute or absent, Portugal won, and his replacement Gonçalo Ramos seized his chance by scoring three goals. Ronaldo was involved only in Portugal’s opening Nations League game, where he was replaced by Ramos in a 1-0 win over Wales. He left the squad after watching the second game from the substitutes’ bench — a 2-1 win in Norway — and Portugal showed no ill effects from his departure with wins over Denmark and Norway to book a quarterfinal. Ronaldo ended the international break with a long post to his 679 million followers on Instagram, where he asked the Portugal coach to acknowledge a mistake in asking him to warm up on the sidelines in Oslo and then not send him on the field. Jesus did not acknowledge any mistake. The star wrote that he expected a suspension under federation rules but promised his fans “we will have one or more farewell matches.” Ronaldo could possibly face a harsh punishment for leaving the training camp. The federation’s disciplinary regulations say that any player who “abandons or fails to appear” without justification at a training session, match or activity of the national teams “shall be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months,” in addition to a fine. Ronaldo did tell the federation he was leaving, but it wasn’t clear whether the decision would be considered justified in accordance with the regulations. “I have already apologized, but I know that actions must have consequences,” Ronaldo wrote in his statement. “Anyone in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.”

articles.title: The rock behind Chelsea's entertainers: Midfield duo key for Blues
articles.summary: The performances of Jordan Henderson and Moises Caicedo underpinned Chelsea's 5-1 victory at home to Bournemouth on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson were paired in midfield for the first time as Chelsea produced their most complete performance of the season.

In a 5-1 victory over Bournemouth on Saturday , manager Xabi Alonso finally found the control and stability required behind his free-scoring attacking trio of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

The Blues have had no problems scoring goals this campaign, with 15 goals from six matches, but no team has conceded more than their total of 13.

Against the Cherries though, Caicedo and Henderson provided the balance to suggest Alonso could finally have found an answer - despite still having to wait for their first clean sheet of the league campaign.

Henderson stole the show by scoring his first two goals for the club. He opened the scoring with a curling effort after 66 seconds before adding a 25-yard free-kick to complete the victory.

Having also set up Rogers for the second goal after just two minutes and 30 seconds, the 36-year-old became the third-oldest player to score and provide an assist in the same match for Chelsea, behind only Didier Drogba and Gianfranco Zola.

Henderson's performance came after a shift in Chelsea's summer recruitment strategy. He arrived on a free transfer from Brentford to add experience to what had been the Premier League's youngest squad.

Alonso said: "We signed him for everything. If he's able to score two beauties like today, we are more than happy for him.

"But apart from the goals, he's done many, many good things. I think today was a very complete performance. We were in control for most of the game, so I'm happy with that. We had good stability in defence as well."

Having not signed a player aged over 30 since Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang in 2022, Chelsea recruited three this summer, with goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez joining from Aston Villa and striker Danny Welbeck also arriving.

Now, recovered from a broken arm sustained while jumping over an advertising hoarding during celebrations following England's win over Mexico at the World Cup, Henderson is showing he is more than just a vocal leader behind the scenes.

Henderson important but Caicedo irreplaceable

There is a strong argument that Chelsea find it easier to cope without the creativity of Cole Palmer than without Caicedo's ability in possession and his knack for breaking up play in midfield.

In his 150th appearance for the club, Caicedo lasted 72 minutes.

His withdrawal for Romeo Lavia was planned, but the Ecuador international still made a significant impact.

Alonso deployed him in a deep role, dropping into the middle of the back three when Chelsea were in possession and allowing young defender Josh Acheampong to push forward.

He misplaced just two passes and recorded the highest pass-completion rate of any Chelsea starter. He also made and won more tackles than any other Chelsea player on Saturday afternoon.

With Caicedo in the side, Chelsea have won 48.1% of their Premier League matches. Without him, that figure drops to 25%.

Alonso said: "You always want to have Moises on the pitch. With him, we have a better midfield area and when you are better in the middle, you have a more complete team.

"I think that is something to build around. With the players that we have up front, they are solid in defence as well. So, I'm happy that Moises is feeling better because he's going to be a key player for us. We knew that."

The alternative options in Chelsea's midfield include captain Reece James, who is able to play in defence, along with substitutes Romeo Lavia and Valentin Barco, who did not make the matchday squad.

It is most likely James who will be attempting to re-take his place from Henderson when back, but the diagnosis on his knee issues remains uncertain.

Chelsea remain a work in progress and conceded again through poor set-piece defending for Evanilson's goal.

However, if Henderson and Caicedo can help eliminate the defensive lapses, Chelsea can begin to look up the table, with Pedro, Rogers and Palmer already helping to make them the Premier League's top scorers.

Alonso said: "I think that they help each other well and they give presence, they give stability.

"You know that they are going to be the ones that are going to be helping the rest, not just for their qualities because they understand the game. They can play in shorter spaces but as well defensively they give good balance."

Former England striker Alan Shearer told BBC Sport: "Caicedo makes a difference. There's no doubt about it. He gives Chelsea a bit more solidity and stops the ball getting into the back four.

"He and Henderson have worked really well, the opening goal being a good example. He definitely makes them more solid, I've been really impressed."

articles.title: Rangers £5M Midfielder Set For 6-Week Injury: Can McInnes Solve His Midfield Crisis?
articles.summary: Rangers will lose Cammy Devlin for around six weeks after the midfielder suffered a hamstring strain during the 1-0 win over Celtic at Parkhead. Derek McInne...
articles.body:
Rangers will lose Cammy Devlin for around six weeks after the midfielder suffered a hamstring strain during the 1-0 win over Celtic at Parkhead. Derek McInnes confirmed the diagnosis on Thursday, while revealing that Devlin will avoid surgery despite his recovery period.

Devlin picked up the problem in the closing stages of the Old Firm victory. Rangers had already used all five substitutions, so the summer signing had to stay on the pitch until the final whistle. Medical checks have established the extent of the injury, leaving McInnes without a midfield option during a demanding run of fixtures.

The timing creates a selection headache. Devlin arrived from Hearts during the summer and had provided another option alongside Dan Neil and Nicolas Raskin . His absence now leaves McInnes with less depth in central midfield, particularly as Rangers prepare to play five matches before the November international break.

How will Rangers manage Cammy Devlin's six-week absence?

Neil and Raskin look likely to carry much of the central midfield workload, although McInnes must avoid pushing either player into unnecessary fatigue. The manager can rotate other positions and use the wider squad to protect his preferred midfield pairing when circumstances allow.

There is some welcome news. Dujon Sterling has returned to training after suffering a minor hamstring issue against Celtic, and McInnes expects him to be available for Saturday's meeting with Kilmarnock. That gives Rangers an important defensive boost after the extended international break.

All 13 players who represented their countries have returned without injury. Minsu Kim collected his first senior caps for South Korea, while Ryan Naderi made his Czech Republic debut, adding another factor to the international workload McInnes must monitor.

Can McInnes protect Rangers during the busy fixture run?

GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – AUGUST 13: Cammy Devlin of Rangers is seen at full time during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 third qualifying round second leg match between Rangers FC and Jagiellonia Bialystok at Ibrox Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

The schedule leaves little room for error. Kilmarnock visit Ibrox on Saturday, followed by matches involving Aberdeen, Hearts, Dundee and St Johnstone, with an Aberdeen semi-final at Hampden among the five fixtures before the next international window.

McInnes can take confidence from Rangers' recent defensive record after six straight wins and back-to-back victories over Celtic. Yet Devlin's injury removes a useful squad piece just as the manager needs fresh legs across several competitions.

The immediate answer should come through sensible rotation rather than a major tactical reshuffle. Neil and Raskin can anchor midfield, while Sterling's return reduces the pressure elsewhere. Rangers now need that balance to hold through a packed spell.

articles.title: Nkunku vuelve a inflar el globo: primer 'hat-trick' en 746 días

articles.summary: El atacante, de vuelta al Leipzig, no marcaba un triplete desde septiembre de 2024
articles.body: Christopher Nkunku está de vuelta. El regreso al RB Leipzig, que le traspasó al Chelsea a cambio de 60 millones de euros en 2023, le ha sentado de maravilla. El internacional francés, de 28 años, ha liderado la goleada sobre el Eintracht Frankfurt (6-0) con un 'hat-trick', el primero que anota en 746 días. Desde el 24 de septiembre de 2024, cuando siendo jugador del Chelsea anotó tres goles en Copa de la Liga contra el AFC Barrow (5-0), no firmaba un triplete. La goleada de los de Martín Demichelis, sin embargo, la inició Ezechiel Banzuzi en el 1'. El internacional congoleño sólo tuvo que rematar en boca de gol un centro desde la derecha de Neil El Aynaoui. El 'show' de Nkunku comenzó en el 5'. Recuperó Antonio Nusa y el francés remató a la red atacando el primer palo. El segundo de su cuenta llegó en el 41', al cazar un rechace de Noah Atubolu a remate de Rômulo. El 'hat-trick' no se hizo esperar. Se concretó en el 44'. Gol, nuevamente, de pillo. Nkunku 'cazó un nuevo mal despeje de Atubolu, esta vez a disparo de Banzuzi. La 'manita' la rubricó Antonio Nusa en el 54'. Banzuzi le lanzó en carrera y el internacional noruego resolvió, mano a mano, tras un gran eslalon. El 'set', en el 89', lo firmó Tidiam Gomis. Fue, sin duda, el mejor gol del partido. Recibió en campo propio de Benjamin Henrichs, se giró y echó a correr. Por el camino dejó hasta a cuatro jugadores antes de batir a Atubolu con un tiro cruzado. Golazo. Demichelis, tras un mal inicio, respira. 'Su' Leipzig es quinto con nueve puntos de 15 posibles. VfB Stuttgart goalkeeper Dennis Seimen returned from injury on Saturday, marking his Bundesliga debut with a clean sheet as his side secured a 2-0 away win against SC Paderborn.

What made the occasion even more special was that the 20-year-old made his first appearance in Germany's top flight against Paderborn, where he spent last season on loan.

"To make my Bundesliga debut for the club where I worked my way through the youth ranks for years – and then to do it against the club I was loaned to last season... These are the kinds of stories that only football can write," Seimen told Sky after the game.

"I have to say, a few tears were shed after the final whistle," Seimen revealed, later telling DAZN that it was "the most emotional experience I have had in my career."

The 20-year-old received a warm reception from the home fans at the Home Deluxe Arena, which meant a lot to him.

"The stadium isn't particularly big, but the fans are still loud. Of course, I noticed it, and it made me incredibly happy," said Seimen, who helped Paderborn secure promotion to the Bundesliga last season.

articles.title: No hay parones en este Barcelona
articles.standfirst: Octavo triunfo en LaLiga y victoria seguida número 23 en el Camp Nou. Flick no echó de menos a Raphinha y reservó a algunos jugadores, pero el resultado final es el mismo: goleada
articles.summary: Octavo triunfo en LaLiga y victoria seguida número 23 en el Camp Nou. Flick no echó de menos a Raphinha y reservó a algunos jugadores, pero el resultado final es el mismo: goleada
articles.body: El larguísimo parón provocó muchos cambios en el once del Barça, pero ningún cambio en el resultado final: una nueva victoria. La octava consecutiva en el arranque de LaLiga y el partido 23 ganando en el Spotify Camp Nou. Hansi Flick no podía contar con Raphinha por lesión y reservó de inicio a Cubarsí, Pedri y Fermín. El que no descansa nunca es un Lamine Yamal sin límites. Pero da lo mismo, juegue quien juegue este equipo es una trituradora de goles y victorias. Su última víctima fue el Getafe, un rival siempre incómodo pero que tampoco tuvo opciones ante el líder. Y no tuvo opciones porque a los 78 segundos de partidos ya había marcado Gordon, con un remate desde fuera del área que rozó en Mario Martín y descolocó a David Soria. Primer gol del inglés con la camiseta azulgrana. El 2-0 de Gabriel Jesus a la media hora dictaba sentencia y Koundé cerró la goleada en la segunda parte. El partido no tuvo color. Si ya es difícil afrontar un partido contra el Barça, verte en desventaja en el marcado antes del segundo minutos tiene que ser desesperante. El Getafe, más pendiente de si llega o no Carvajal al equipo, cerró líneas desde el gol y su misión pasó a ser no acabar goleado. Gordon, que ha crecido como jugador una barbaridad desde que está en el Barça, puso un centro envenenado al segundo palo que rozó Dani Olmo y obligó a David Soria a lucirse. El 2-0 acechaba. Luego fue Eric García con un lanzamiento lejano el que lo intentó. La tercera fue la vencida. Una sobrada de Zaid Romero intentando regatear jugadores en su área acabó con una pérdida de balón a los pies de Gabriel Jesus, que batió a David Soria con un remate ajustado al primer palo. El brasileño sigue aprovechando los minutos que tiene y la baja de Raphinha no se hizo notar ni en ataque ni en defensa ante los azulones. La mala suerte de Romero no acabó ahí y tuvo que ser sustituido por lesión unos minutos después. Otra baja importante para el jueves europeo de los de Bordalás. Sin necesidad de apretar el acelerador, el Barça tuvo opción del tercero en el añadido de la primera mitad, pero Koundé no acertó a controlar cuando estaba solo ante Soria. La segunda mitad comenzó sin cambios. El Geta se la jugó en los primeros minutos buscando un gol que le metiera en el partido y Mojica lo intentó con un remate lejano que se fue fuera por poco. El ritmo de juego bajó en este periodo. Al Barça no le hacía falta apretar y el Getafe no podía por lo que la calidad tomó el mando en el partido y ahí lo de Flick golean. Las ocasiones llegaban con cuentagotas, pero siempre en la misma portería. Gordon, muy activo, estuvo a punto de llegar a un pase al hueco hacia el, pero Soria se le adelantó en una jugada en la que chocaron sus rodillas, pero no hubo que lamentar nada reseñable. El meta azulón volvió a ser decisivo ante un remate de Dani Olmo. A falta de media hora Flick comenzó a mover el banquillo y dio entrada a Pedri y Fermín. Y con la entrada de ambos, el Barcelona recuperó la chispa. No era el día del Getafe y Andrés García también dejó el terreno de juego con molestias. El que no acababa de aparecer era Lamine Yamal, los pegajosos marcajes getafenses impedían su lucimiento y no se le veía cómodo. Pero Lamine siempre está aunque no lo parezca y el 10 fue quien puso en bandeja el 3-0 a Koundé con un pase marca de la casa. El francés celebró con gol el jugador galo con más partidos en la historia del Barça. La goleada iba tomando forma. Con los tres al Getafe, los del Barcelona sumaban 34 y casi doblan al segundo equipo más goleador de LaLiga que es el Atlético con 18. Unos números que asustan a cualquiera. Tuvieron minutos también Adeyemi y Bernal y hasta el egipcio Hamza, que promete mucho. El Barça sigue a lo suyo ganando todo lo que juega y llega más que preparado para ese cercano Clásico que puede abrir más brecha con el Real Madrid, aunque por delante aun tendrá al Galatasaray y al Betis, que no serán fáciles. El Geta puede dar por bueno el 3-0 con todas las bajas que tenía y su guerra estará el jueves en su estreno en la fase liga de la Conference en Rumanía.

articles.title: Ni Flick podía imaginarse algo así
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Barcelona-Getafe
articles.body: La sensación del Barcelona en los primeros partidos de esta temporada ha sido, sin ninguna duda, Raphinha, con 14 goles anotados. Había ciertas dudas ante su ausencia por lesión en el partido frente al Getafe. Nada de nada. El equipo de Flick sigue siendo una máquina de marcar goles, y así lo demostró frente al Getafe. Si no está Raphinha, ahí aparecen Gordon y Gabriel Jesus. Además, lo hacen por la vía rápida, porque apenas se había cumplido el primer minuto cuando el inglés abrió la cuenta, estrenándose como goleador. Luego fue el turno de Gabriel Jesus, que jugaba en el puesto de Raphinha y marcó su tercer gol de la temporada. De brasileño a brasileño. Está claro que el Barcelona ha fichado bien. Había miedo de que las salidas de Lewandowski, Ferran y Rashford pasaran factura al equipo azulgrana. La realidad es que ya nadie se acuerda de estos tres jugadores y que el Barcelona ha sabido cubrir sus bajas con las incorporaciones de Gordon, Adeyemi y Gabriel Jesus. Los tres ya han marcado esta temporada, contribuyendo al excelente nivel de Raphinha y Lamine Yamal. Y la noche la redondeó Koundé. Ni Flick podía imaginar que esto le iba a salir tan bien. Sobre todo, que haciendo un partido normalito ganasen por 3-0. Nueve de nueve. Antes del partido, Pedro Rodríguez tuvo la oportunidad de despedirse del Camp Nou. El canario había anunciado esta semana que se retiraba del fútbol y pudo decir adiós a la afición que lleva en el corazón. Aunque ha jugado en muchos equipos, sus mejores años los vivió en el cuadro azulgrana. La ovación que recibió por parte de la afición fue más que merecida. Partido después del parón y tocaban rotaciones. Flick lo tenía claro y dejó fuera del equipo a Raphinha (no quiso forzar en ningún momento su regreso), Cubarsí, Pedri y Fermín. Hay que dosificar los minutos porque lo que viene en las próximas semanas es de órdago. En los próximos siete días, dos partidos fuera de casa y, después, la semana grande, con el PSG y el Real Madrid. Empieza a ser un espectáculo ver jugar a Rodri. Es un futbolista que no hace ruido ni tiene los focos puestos encima como Lamine o Raphinha, pero su puesta en escena es excelente. Su precisión en el pase es absoluta y también destaca a la hora de recuperar balones. Pero, sobre todo, sabe marcar el ritmo del partido. Acelera cuando toca y ralentiza el juego si es necesario. Soberbio. No tiene suerte Dani Olmo. Frente al Getafe volvió a realizar un buen partido, asociándose muy bien con el resto de sus compañeros, especialmente con Gabriel Jesus. Pero, a la hora de marcar, es otra cosa. Poco antes de ser sustituido, Xavi Espart le puso un balón perfecto que lo dejó solo delante de Soria, pero su disparo fue rechazado por el guardameta. Todavía no ha marcado esta temporada.

articles.title: Man City charges: Manchester United fans take aim at rivals with return of famous ticker banner
articles.summary: Man Utd fans' famous banner mocking the years since Man City won a trophy returned to Old Trafford on Saturday; United were playing first game since City were found guilty of all serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission
articles.body:
The banner was first displayed in 2000, at which point it was 24 years since City last won a trophy - the 1976 League Cup.

The year listed on the banner ticked over every year until 2011, when City ended their trophy drought by beating Stoke in the FA Cup final - their first silverware since Sheikh Mansour's takeover.

But after City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission, United fans took aim at their rivals by displaying a new version of the banner for the visit of Tottenham.

It marks 50 years since City won the 1976 League Cup, therefore discounting the eight Premier Leagues, four FA Cups, seven League Cups, four Community Shields, one Champions League, one Super Cup and one Club World Cup they have won since the takeover.

City deny wrongdoing and lodged an appeal against the commission's findings. The commission's findings specifically related to the period between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons.

United fans also displayed a banner of Rui Pinto with the caption 'computer genius'. Pinto is a convicted hacker who obtained emails that formed the basis of articles published by Der Spiegel in 2018 that first alleged financial breaches by City.

United's game against Tottenham was their first since the news of the independent commission's judgement was revealed.

City play for the first time since the news broke on Sunday, away to Liverpool, live on Sky Sports .
